label: thm:SG
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:SG}
Every \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor with separable predual is generated, as a von Neumann algebra, by two self-adjoint elements.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Let \(A\) be a separable unital \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}-algebra such that $\partial\mathrm{T}(A)$ is nonempty, compact, and zero-dimensional. Assume that \textup{(C)} (\eqref{eq:comparison}) holds. Then
\[
A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(g_1,g_2)
\]
for two ordinary elements \(g_1,g_2\in A\).
head: environment

label: gr:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{gr:main}
Let \(A\) be a separable unital \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}-algebra such that $\partial\mathrm{T}(A)$ is nonempty, compact, and zero-dimensional. Assume that $A$ has real rank zero, and assume that \textup{(PC)} (\eqref{eq:PC}) holds. Then $A$ is singly generated, and its single generators form a norm-dense \(G_\delta\) subset of \(A\). Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{gr}(A)\leq1,
\]
with equality when \(A\) is noncommutative, where $\operatorname{gr}$ is Thiel's generator rank in \cite{ThielGR}.
head: environment

label: thm:polar
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:polar}
Let \(A\) be a separable unital \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}-algebra such that
\(\partial\mathrm{T}(A)\) is nonempty, compact, and zero-dimensional.
Assume that \(A\) satisfies \textup{(C)}.
Suppose there is a unitary \(u\in A\) with the following properties.
For \(\tau\in\partial\mathrm{T}(A)\), put
\[
M_\tau=\pi_\tau(A)'',\qquad u_\tau=\pi_\tau(u),\qquad
D_\tau=\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(u_\tau),
\]
and let \(\mathbb E_{D_\tau}:M_\tau\to D_\tau\) be the trace-preserving
conditional expectation. For every \(\tau\in\partial\mathrm{T}(A)\),
\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{u-cond-1} the spectral distribution of \(u\) with respect
  to \(\tau\) is atomless and has full support on \(\mathbb T\); and
\item\label{u-cond-2} for every \(a\in A\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-compression}
\lim_{t\downarrow0}
\sup_{\substack{p\in D_\tau\ {\rm projection}\\
                 0<\tau(p)\leq t}}
\left\|p\bigl(\pi_\tau(a)-\mathbb E_{D_\tau}(\pi_\tau(a))\bigr)p\right\|=0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Then there are \(h=h^*\in A\) and \(R>\left\|h\right\|\) such that
\[
A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(u(R1+h)).
\]
head: environment

label: cor:free-product
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:free-product}
Let \((A_0,\tau_0)\) and \((B,\sigma)\) be separable unital
\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}-algebras with faithful tracial states. Suppose that \(A_0\)
contains a \(\tau_0\)-Haar unitary \(u\) satisfying
Condition~\ref{u-cond-2} in its GNS representation, with
\(D=\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(\pi_{\tau_0}(u))\), and that \(B\) contains a unitary
\(v\) with \(\sigma(v)=0\). Then the reduced free product
\[
 (A_0,\tau_0)*(B,\sigma)
\]
is singly generated.
head: environment

label: cor:free-single
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:free-single}
For every \(n\in\{2,3,\ldots,\infty\}\), both
\(\mathrm{C}_r^*(\mathbb F_n)\) and the reduced free product of
\(n\) copies of \((\mathrm{C}([0,1]),\lambda)\) are singly
generated, where \(\lambda\) is Lebesgue measure.
head: environment

label: cor:parameter
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:parameter}
Let \(B\) satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:polar}
with \(\mathrm{T}(B)=\{\tau\}\), and let \(X\) be a nonempty compact
metrizable zero-dimensional space. Then \(\mathrm{C}(X,B)\) is singly
generated. In particular, this applies when \(B\) is any of the
reduced free products in Corollary~\ref{cor:free-product}, including
the free-group and interval examples in Corollary~\ref{cor:free-single}.

title: Proof

Put $p=1\otimes e_{11}$ and choose a stabilized witness $w$ with
$\left\|w^*(b\otimes e_{11})w-a\otimes e_{11}\right\|<\eta$.
Its $(1,1)$ compression satisfies
\[
p w^*(b\otimes e_{11})w p

label: lem:markov
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In $M$, the support projection of $\pi((d-\varepsilon)_+)$ is
$1_{(\varepsilon,\infty)}(\pi(d))$. Since
$\pi(d)^2\geq\varepsilon^2 1_{(\varepsilon,\infty)}(\pi(d))$,
taking traces gives the positive-sign estimate. Apply the same argument
to $-d$ for the other sign.
For the second assertion, the scalar function
$t\mapsto t-(t-\varepsilon)_++(-t-\varepsilon)_+$ has absolute value
at most $\varepsilon$. Apply continuous functional calculus.

label: lem:lift
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lift}
Let $q:D\to E$ be a surjective unital $*$-homomorphism of unital
$\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebras. Every $b\in E_\mathrm{sa}$ with $\left\|b\right\|\leq R$ has a
self-adjoint lift $h\in D_\mathrm{sa}$ with $\left\|h\right\|\leq R$.
Consequently, $q:D_\mathrm{sa}\to E_\mathrm{sa}$ is open for the norm topologies.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take an arbitrary self-adjoint lift $h_0$, obtained by symmetrizing a
lift of $b$. The continuous truncation
$\chi_R(t)=\max\{-R,\min\{t,R\}\}$ satisfies
$q(\chi_R(h_0))=\chi_R(b)=b$ and
$\left\|\chi_R(h_0)\right\|\leq R$. Lifting each element of an open ball
with its own norm bound proves openness.
head: environment

label: lem:polynomial
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:polynomial}
Let $M$ be a finite tracial von Neumann algebra. On every
operator-norm-bounded set of tuples, evaluation of a fixed noncommutative
$*$-polynomial is continuous for the $2$-norm.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For a word of length $d$ in tuples whose entries have norm at most $R$,
replace its factors one at a time. The inequalities
$\left\|azb\right\|_2\leq\left\|a\right\|\left\|z\right\|_2\left\|b\right\|$ give
\[
\left\|w(s)-w(t)\right\|_2\leq
d\max\{1,R\}^{d-1}\max_i\left\|s_i-t_i\right\|_2.
\]
Apply this to the finitely many words in the polynomial; adjoints
preserve the $2$-norm.

label: lem:separated-fibres
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:separated-fibres}
Let \(A\) be separable and unital, with
\(\varnothing\neq K=\partial\mathrm{T}(A)\) compact and zero-dimensional.
Let \(C\subseteq A\) be a unital sub-\(\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}\)-algebra such that
\[
\pi_\tau(C)''=\pi_\tau(A)''\quad(\tau\in K),
\]
and suppose that \(\tau\mapsto\tau|_C\) is injective on \(K\).
Then, for every \(z\in A_\mathrm{sa}\) with \(\left\|z\right\|\leq1\) and
every \(\eta>0\), there is \(c\in C_\mathrm{sa}\) such that
\[
\left\|c\right\|\leq1,\qquad \left\|z-c\right\|_{2,K}<\eta.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Each restricted trace is extremal, because its GNS von Neumann
algebra is the factor \(\pi_\tau(A)''\). Thus the restriction
map identifies \(K\) with a compact subset \(K_C\) of
\(\partial\mathrm{T}(C)\). Let \(F_C\) be the closed Bauer face generated
by \(K_C\), and complete \(C\) relative to \(F_C\).
The inclusion into \(\mathcal M_K\) extends to an injective
\(*\)-homomorphism
\[
\Phi:\mathcal M_{C,F_C}\longrightarrow\mathcal M_K.
\]
Indeed, the uniform \(2\)-seminorms on \(C\) agree, and bounded
uniformly \(2\)-Cauchy sequences give the extension. Unit-ball
density makes it contractive; equality of the \(2\)-norms makes
it injective and hence isometric.

By \cite[Theorem 3.37]{TracialComplete}, the source contains
\(\mathrm{C}(K_C)\) centrally. Its function corresponding to
\(f\in \mathrm{C}(K)\) has scalar image \(f(\tau)1\) in every factor
fibre. The family of extended traces on \(\mathcal M_K\) is
faithful, so its image is the ambient central function \(f\).
In particular, the range of \(\Phi\) contains every central
clopen projection.

For each \(\tau\in K\), the Kaplansky density theorem in each fibre and
Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} give a self-adjoint contraction
\(c_\tau\in C\) with \(\left\|z-c_\tau\right\|_{2,\tau}<\eta/4\).
The inequality with \(\eta/2\) holds on a neighborhood of
\(\tau\). Choose a subordinate finite clopen partition
\(V_1,\ldots,V_L\), let \(p_\ell=1_{V_\ell}\), and choose the
corresponding contractions \(c_\ell\). Then
\[
d=\sum_\ell p_\ell c_\ell\in\Phi(\mathcal M_{C,F_C}),
\qquad \left\|d\right\|\leq1,
\qquad \left\|z-d\right\|_{2,K}<\eta/2.
\]
Approximate the self-adjoint contractive preimage of \(d\)
by a self-adjoint contraction from \(C\), using
\cite[Proposition 3.28]{TracialComplete} and quotient lifting.
An error smaller than \(\eta/2\) proves the assertion.

label: gr:lem:projection-pair
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:lem:projection-pair}
Using Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}, every finite factor $M$ with separable
predual has a projection $P$ and a self-adjoint contraction $D$ such
that $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(P,D)=M$.  If $M\neq\mathbb C$, one may require
$0<P<1$.  For $M=\mathbb C$, take $P=1$ and $D=0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $M=\mathrm{M}_d(\mathbb C)$, $d\geq2$, choose distinct
$t_1,\ldots,t_d\in[0,1]$, let $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_d)$,
and let $P$ be the rank-one projection onto
$d^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1)$.  Spectral calculus for $D$ gives each diagonal
matrix unit, and $e_{ii}Pe_{jj}=d^{-1}e_{ij}$ gives all matrix units.

Suppose instead that $M$ is type $\mathrm{II}_1$.  Splitting its identity into
two equivalent projections identifies $M$ with $\mathrm{M}_2(N)$, where $N$ is
a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual.  Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}
gives $u,v\in N_\mathrm{sa}$ with $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(u,v)=N$.  Affine rescaling allows us
to assume $3/5\leq u,v\leq4/5$.  Set
\[
 s=(u-u^2)^{1/2},\qquad
 P=\begin{pmatrix}1-u&s\\s&u\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 D=\begin{pmatrix}v&0\\0&1/2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since $s$ commutes with $u$ and $s^2=u-u^2$, we have
$P=P^*=P^2$.  Both $P$ and $1-P$ are nonzero, and $D$ is a
self-adjoint contraction.  The separated spectra of $v$ and $1/2$
recover $e_{11}$ and $e_{22}$ from $D$.  Moreover, $s$ is positive
and invertible, so the polar part of $e_{11}Pe_{22}$ is $e_{12}$.
These matrix units, the $e_{22}$ compression of $P$, and the
$e_{11}$ compression of $D$ recover $u$ and $v$ in the first corner.
They therefore generate $\mathrm{M}_2(N)$ as a von Neumann algebra.

label: gr:lem:join
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:lem:join}
Let $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ be nonzero orthogonal projections summing to
the identity of a finite factor $M$.  Suppose a von Neumann
subalgebra $E\subseteq M$ contains $f_jMf_j$ for every $j$ and a
nonzero element of $f_jMf_{j+1}$ for every $j<s$.  Then $E=M$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a nonzero element of $f_jMf_{j+1}$ lying in $E$, and let
$v\in E$ be its polar part.  Its initial projection
$q=v^*v\leq f_{j+1}$ is nonzero, and $vv^*\leq f_j$.
Finite-factor comparison supplies finitely many partial isometries
$t_i\in f_{j+1}Mf_{j+1}$ such that
\[
 t_i^*t_i\leq q,\qquad \sum_i t_it_i^*=f_{j+1}.
\]
Indeed, partition $f_{j+1}$ into finitely many projections whose
traces are at most the trace of $q$, and compare each of them with
$q$.  Such a partition exists by the elementary dimension theory
of matrix and type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.  For $y\in f_jMf_{j+1}$,
\[
 y=\sum_i (yt_iv^*)(vt_i^*).
\]
Here $yt_iv^*\in f_jMf_j\subseteq E$ and $vt_i^*\in E$, proving
$f_jMf_{j+1}\subseteq E$.  Taking adjoints gives the reverse corner.

To obtain every remaining corner, join successively larger diagonal
corners.  More explicitly, if $F=f_1+\cdots+f_j$ and
$FMF\subseteq E$, the already recovered nonzero element of
$f_jMf_{j+1}\subseteq FMf_{j+1}$ and the same argument give
$FMf_{j+1}\subseteq E$.  Hence
$(F+f_{j+1})M(F+f_{j+1})\subseteq E$.  Induction gives $E=M$.

label: gr:common-labels
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:common-labels}
Fix distinct real numbers $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_L$, a number
$C\geq0$, and $\rho>0$.  There are an integer $N\geq1$ and
pairwise distinct nonzero real labels
\[
 \Lambda_\ell=\{\lambda_{\ell,k,+},\lambda_{\ell,k,-}:1\leq k\leq N\},
 \qquad 1\leq\ell\leq L,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}\label{gr:eq:labels}
 |\lambda-\alpha_\ell|<\rho\quad(\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell),
 \qquad
 R=\left|\bigcup_{\ell=1}^L\Lambda_\ell\right|=2LN,
\end{equation}
with the following property.  Let $M$ be any finite factor with
separable predual, let $e_1,\ldots,e_L$ be orthogonal projections
in $M$ summing to $1$, and let $B_0\in M_\mathrm{sa}$ satisfy
$\left\|B_0\right\|\leq C$.  Some $e_\ell$ may be zero.  There are
$H,B\in M_\mathrm{sa}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
 $H=\sum_{\ell,k,\sigma}\lambda_{\ell,k,\sigma}e_{\ell,k,\sigma}$,
 where the projections are orthogonal and
 $\sum_{k,\sigma}e_{\ell,k,\sigma}=e_\ell$;
\item
 $\left\|H-\sum_\ell\alpha_\ell e_\ell\right\|<\rho$ and
 $\left\|B-B_0\right\|<\rho$;
\item $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(H,B)=M$.
\end{enumerate}
Zero projections in the refined partition are allowed.  The integer
$N$ may be chosen using only $C$ and $\rho$; all labels are fixed
using only $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_L,C,\rho$.  In particular, neither
the labels nor $R$ depends on $M$, the projection partition, a target
element, or a tracial approximation tolerance.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $C>0$, choose $N>8C/\rho$ and partition $[-C,C]$ into $N$
nonempty Borel intervals $I_k$ of diameter $2C/N<\rho/4$.
Allocate every common endpoint to just one interval.  Choose
$\mu_k\in I_k$.  If $C=0$, take $N=1$, $I_1=\{0\}$, and
$\mu_1=0$.  Choose the $2LN$ labels in advance, all distinct and
nonzero, with each $\Lambda_\ell$ contained in a sufficiently small
neighborhood of $\alpha_\ell$ to satisfy
\eqref{gr:eq:labels}.  The neighborhoods for different $\ell$ can
be chosen disjoint, because the $\alpha_\ell$ are distinct.

For each nonzero $e_\ell$, use Borel functional calculus in its
corner to set
\[
 f_{\ell,k}=1_{I_k}(e_\ell B_0e_\ell).
\]
These projections sum to $e_\ell$ and satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{gr:eq:diagonal-bound}
 \left\|f_{\ell,k}B_0f_{\ell,k}-\mu_kf_{\ell,k}\right\|<\rho/4
\end{equation}
whenever $f_{\ell,k}\neq0$.  If $e_\ell=0$, set all
$f_{\ell,k}=0$.  Every nonzero corner $f_{\ell,k}Mf_{\ell,k}$
is a finite factor.  By Lemma~\ref{gr:lem:projection-pair}, choose
a projection $P_{\ell,k}$ and a self-adjoint contraction
$D_{\ell,k}$ generating this corner.  If it is scalar, take
$P_{\ell,k}=f_{\ell,k}$ and $D_{\ell,k}=0$.  Set
\[
 e_{\ell,k,+}=P_{\ell,k},\qquad
 e_{\ell,k,-}=f_{\ell,k}-P_{\ell,k},
\]
and set these projections to zero for zero corners.  Define $H$
using the predetermined labels and this refined partition.  Its
norm estimate follows directly from \eqref{gr:eq:labels}.

Choose $0<\gamma<\rho/4$.  Replace each nonzero diagonal
compression of $B_0$ onto $f_{\ell,k}$ by
\[
 \mu_kf_{\ell,k}+\gamma D_{\ell,k},
\]
retaining all off-diagonal compressions.  By
\eqref{gr:eq:diagonal-bound}, this block diagonal change has norm
less than $\rho/2$.  Enumerate the nonzero $f_{\ell,k}$ as
$f_1,\ldots,f_s$.  Whenever a successive compression
$f_jBf_{j+1}$ is zero, insert a nonzero element of arbitrarily small
norm in that corner and its adjoint in the reverse corner.  Each
such corner is nonzero because $M$ is a factor.  There are finitely
many insertions, so their total norm can be made less than
$\rho/2$.  They do not alter diagonal compressions.  The resulting
self-adjoint $B$ satisfies $\left\|B-B_0\right\|<\rho$ and
$f_jBf_{j+1}\neq0$ for every $j<s$.

Spectral calculus for $H$ recovers every nonzero
$e_{\ell,k,\sigma}$, because the labels are all distinct, and
therefore recovers $f_{\ell,k}$ and $P_{\ell,k}$.  Compression of
$B$ then recovers
\[
 D_{\ell,k}
 =\gamma^{-1}\bigl(f_{\ell,k}Bf_{\ell,k}-\mu_kf_{\ell,k}\bigr).
\]
Thus $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(H,B)$ contains every full diagonal corner and every
successive nonzero link.  Lemma~\ref{gr:lem:join} proves that it
equals $M$.

label: gr:rem:label-quantifiers
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{gr:rem:label-quantifiers}
For the pair in Lemma~\ref{gr:common-labels}, every
$X\in M_\mathrm{sa}$ and every $\delta>0$ admit a self-adjoint
noncommutative polynomial $P$ such that
\[
 \left\|X-P(H,B)\right\|_{2,\tau_M}<\delta.
\]
Indeed, the Kaplansky density theorem gives a bounded self-adjoint approximant
from $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,H,B)$, and norm approximation in that algebra gives a
self-adjoint polynomial.  The polynomial may depend on $X$,
$\delta$, and the chosen pair.  The labels and their cardinality
$R$ do not.  Since the labels are nonzero, $H$ is invertible; thus
adjoining $1$ makes no difference to the algebra generated by $H,B$.

label: prop:ambient
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ambient}
In a finite factor $M$ with separable predual,
self-adjoint pairs $(H,B)$ satisfying $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(H,B)=M$ are norm dense
in $M_\mathrm{sa}^2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $a,b\in M_\mathrm{sa}$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Bounded Borel functional
calculus gives $a_0=\sum_\ell\alpha_\ell p_\ell$ of finite spectrum
with $\left\|a-a_0\right\|<\varepsilon/2$. Apply
Lemma~\ref{gr:common-labels} to these scalar labels, $B_0=b$,
$C=\left\|b\right\|$, and $\rho=\varepsilon/2$. It supplies a weakly
generating pair with $\left\|H-a_0\right\|<\varepsilon/2$ and
$\left\|B-b\right\|<\varepsilon/2$, as required. The construction includes
matrix and scalar factors.
head: environment

label: prop:transfer
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:transfer}
Using Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}, let $A$ be a separable unital
$\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebra with a tracial state $\tau$ and suppose
$M=\pi_\tau(A)''$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. The set
\[
\{(x,y)\in A_\mathrm{sa}^2:\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(\pi_\tau(x),\pi_\tau(y))=M\}
\]
is a norm-dense $G_\delta$ in $A_\mathrm{sa}^2$, without simplicity or faithfulness.
head: environment

label: eq:baire-condition
title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\pi=\pi_\tau$ and choose a countable norm-dense set $(z_j)$ in
$A_\mathrm{sa}$. For $j,k\geq1$ let $U_{jk}$ consist of the pairs $(a,b)$ for
which some self-adjoint $*$-polynomial $P$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:baire-condition}
\left\|z_j-P(a,b)\right\|_2<1/k.
\end{equation}
These sets are norm open, since polynomial evaluation is norm continuous
and $\left\|c\right\|_2\leq\left\|c\right\|$ also for the trace seminorm.

Fix $(a,b)\in A_\mathrm{sa}^2$ and $\rho>0$.
Proposition~\ref{prop:ambient} supplies a generating pair $(H,K)$ in
$M_\mathrm{sa}^2$ such that
\[
\left\|H-\pi(a)\right\|<\rho/4,\qquad
\left\|K-\pi(b)\right\|<\rho/4.
\]
Choose a self-adjoint polynomial $P$ with
$\left\|\pi(z_j)-P(H,K)\right\|_2<1/(2k)$.
The Kaplansky density theorem in $B=\pi(A)$ provides self-adjoint
$\bar c,\bar d\in B$ of norm at most $\rho/4$, approximating
$H-\pi(a),K-\pi(b)$ arbitrarily closely in $2$-norm.
Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} supplies self-adjoint lifts $c,d\in A$ with
$\left\|c\right\|,\left\|d\right\|\leq\rho/4$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:polynomial}, applied in $M$, makes the lifts satisfy
\[
\left\|P(\pi(a+c),\pi(b+d))-P(H,K)\right\|_2<1/(2k).
\]
Here $2$-norm convergence follows from bounded strong convergence by
evaluating at the trace vector. Thus $(a+c,b+d)\in U_{jk}$ and lies
in the prescribed norm neighborhood. Every $U_{jk}$ is dense.

Baire's theorem makes $\bigcap_{j,k}U_{jk}$ a norm-dense $G_\delta$.
For a pair $(x,y)$ in this intersection, put
$Q=\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(\pi(x),\pi(y))$. Condition \eqref{eq:baire-condition} places
every $\pi(z_j)$ in $L^2(Q,\tau)$. The trace-preserving conditional
expectation $\mathbb E_Q:M\to Q$ fixes all these elements and, by norm density,
all of $B$. Consequently $B\subset Q$ and $Q=M$.
Conversely, the Kaplansky density theorem followed by polynomial norm
approximation shows that every weakly generating pair satisfies all the conditions.
This identifies the intersection with the displayed locus.

label: lem:bauer-pair
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:bauer-pair}
Using Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}, let $A$ be a separable unital
$\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebra with $\mathrm{T}(A)\neq\varnothing$.  Suppose
$K=\partial\mathrm{T}(A)$ is compact and zero-dimensional.  Then a norm-dense
$G_\delta$ subset of $A_\mathrm{sa}^2$ consists of pairs $(x,y)$ for which
\begin{enumerate}
\item the function $\tau\mapsto\tau(x)$ is injective on $K$;
\item $\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(\pi_\tau(x),\pi_\tau(y))=\pi_\tau(A)''$ for every
      $\tau\in K$; and
\item if $C=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,x,y)$, then for every $z\in A_\mathrm{sa}$ with
      $\left\|z\right\|\leq1$ and every $\eta>0$, there is $c\in C_\mathrm{sa}$
      with $\left\|c\right\|\leq1$ and $\left\|z-c\right\|_{2,K}<\eta$.
\end{enumerate}
If every extremal GNS factor is a matrix algebra, the lemma does not
use Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the uniform completion
$\mathcal M_A=\mathcal M_K$ and canonical map $\iota$ described in
Section~\ref{sec:prelim}. Its extended traces form a faithful
family and its canonical central functions act fiberwise as
scalars. Compactness of $K$ identifies
$\operatorname{Aff}(\mathrm{T}(A))$ with $\mathrm{C}(K,\mathbb R)$ by restriction.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{A generic first coordinate separates the traces.}
Consider the bounded real-linear map
\[
 E:A_\mathrm{sa}\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}(K,\mathbb R),\qquad
 E(a)(\tau)=\tau(a).
\]
It is an open surjection.  Indeed, a continuous real function on $K$
extends to a continuous affine function on $\mathrm{T}(A)$, and
\cite[Proposition 2.7]{TracialComplete} gives, for every such function
$f$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, an $a\in A_\mathrm{sa}$ satisfying
$E(a)=f$ and $\left\|a\right\|\leq\left\|f\right\|_\infty+\varepsilon$.

Fix a compatible metric $\rho$ on $K$.  For $m\geq1$, let $V_m$
consist of those $f\in \mathrm{C}(K,\mathbb R)$ such that
\[
 f(\tau)\neq f(\sigma)
 \quad\text{whenever }\rho(\tau,\sigma)\geq1/m.
\]
This set is open: the indicated pairs form a compact subset of
$K\times K$, and the continuous function
$|f(\tau)-f(\sigma)|$ has a positive minimum there when that subset
is nonempty.  It is also dense.  Given $f$ and a prescribed uniform
error, choose a finite clopen partition on whose cells both the
oscillation of $f$ and the diameter for $\rho$ are sufficiently
small, with every diameter less than $1/m$.  Approximate $f$ by a
function constant on each cell, choosing the finitely many constants
distinct by arbitrarily small perturbations.  The resulting function
belongs to $V_m$.  Thus
\[
 S=\bigcap_{m\geq1}E^{-1}(V_m)
\]
is a norm-dense $G_\delta$ subset of $A_\mathrm{sa}$; its elements have
injective trace-evaluation functions.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{A generic pair generates every fiber.}
Choose a countable norm-dense sequence $(z_j)$ in the self-adjoint
unit ball of $A$.  Fix a countable collection $\mathcal P$ of
self-adjoint noncommutative $*$-polynomials in two self-adjoint
variables, with rational real and imaginary coefficients, which is
dense among such polynomials on every norm-bounded set of pairs.
For $j,k\geq1$, let $U_{jk}\subseteq A_\mathrm{sa}^2$ consist of the pairs
$(a,b)$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bauer-local-polynomials}
 \text{for every }\tau\in K\text{ there is }P\in\mathcal P
 \text{ with }\left\|z_j-P(a,b)\right\|_{2,\tau}<1/k.
\end{equation}
Each $U_{jk}$ is norm open.  For a pair satisfying
\eqref{eq:bauer-local-polynomials}, continuity in $\tau$ gives a
neighborhood on which any chosen polynomial witness still works.
Compactness supplies finitely many witnesses.  Equivalently, for
some $P_1,\ldots,P_L\in\mathcal P$,
\[
 \max_{\tau\in K}\min_{1\leq\ell\leq L}
 \left\|z_j-P_\ell(a,b)\right\|_{2,\tau}<1/k.
\]
The expression is norm continuous in $(a,b)$, so the strict inequality
persists under small norm perturbations.

We next prove density.  Fix $(a,b)\in A_\mathrm{sa}^2$ and $r>0$.
For every $\tau\in K$ there is a pair
$(a_\tau,b_\tau)\in A_\mathrm{sa}^2$ within $r/4$ of $(a,b)$ in each
coordinate and generating $M_\tau$ weakly.  When $M_\tau$ is
$\mathrm{II}_1$, this is Proposition~\ref{prop:transfer}.
When $M_\tau=\mathrm{M}_n$, the image $\pi_\tau(A)$ equals $\mathrm{M}_n$.
Perturb the first self-adjoint matrix to have distinct eigenvalues,
and perturb the second to have nonzero entries between consecutive
eigenvectors.  The perturbed pair generates $\mathrm{M}_n$; lifting the two
small self-adjoint differences by Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} gives the
assertion in $A$.  For $n=1$ no perturbation is needed.

Choose $P_\tau\in\mathcal P$ with
\[
 \left\|z_j-P_\tau(a_\tau,b_\tau)\right\|_{2,\tau}<1/(4k).
\]
This follows from weak generation and the Kaplansky density theorem, followed by
polynomial approximation.  The same pair and polynomial have error
less than $1/(2k)$ on an open neighborhood of $\tau$.  A finite
clopen partition $V_1,\ldots,V_L$ can be chosen subordinate to a
finite collection of these neighborhoods.  Write $(a_\ell,b_\ell)$
and $P_\ell$ for the corresponding pairs and polynomials, and let
$p_\ell\in \mathrm{C}(K)\subseteq Z(\mathcal M_A)$ be the characteristic
function of $V_\ell$.  Set
\[
 H_0=\sum_{\ell=1}^L p_\ell\iota(a_\ell),\qquad
 K_0=\sum_{\ell=1}^L p_\ell\iota(b_\ell).
\]
These are self-adjoint, and orthogonality of the central projections
gives
\[
 \left\|H_0-\iota(a)\right\|<r/4,\qquad
 \left\|K_0-\iota(b)\right\|<r/4.
\]
Moreover, the fiber of $(H_0,K_0)$ at any $\tau\in V_\ell$ is the
fiber of $(a_\ell,b_\ell)$, so its $P_\ell$ error is less than
$1/(2k)$.

Bounded uniform tracial density supplies self-adjoint $u,v\in A$
with $\left\|u\right\|,\left\|v\right\|\leq r/4$ such that
$\iota(a+u),\iota(b+v)$ are as close as desired to $H_0,K_0$ in the
uniform $2$-norm.  One can obtain self-adjoint approximants by
symmetrizing the bounded approximants.  Lemma~\ref{lem:polynomial}
applies uniformly over the fibers, since its estimate depends only
on the polynomial and the operator-norm bound.  Thus these
approximants can be chosen so that the error in each of the finitely
many $P_\ell$ evaluations is less than $1/(2k)$ uniformly on $K$.
The pair $(a+u,b+v)$ then belongs to $U_{jk}$ and to the prescribed
norm neighborhood.  This proves density of $U_{jk}$.

Baire's theorem now gives a norm-dense $G_\delta$
\[
 \mathcal G=(S\times A_\mathrm{sa})\cap\bigcap_{j,k\geq1}U_{jk}.
\]
For $(x,y)\in\mathcal G$ and a fixed $\tau\in K$, put
$Q_\tau=\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(\pi_\tau(x),\pi_\tau(y))\subseteq M_\tau$.
The defining conditions put every $\pi_\tau(z_j)$ in
$L^2(Q_\tau,\tau)$.  The trace-preserving conditional expectation
$\mathbb E_{Q_\tau}:M_\tau\to Q_\tau$ therefore fixes these elements, hence all of
$\pi_\tau(A)$ by norm density and rescaling.  Consequently
$Q_\tau=M_\tau$.  This proves the first two assertions.

Put \(C=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,x,y)\). The restricted traces are distinct because
their values on \(x\) are distinct, and the fibrewise generation
has just been proved. Lemma~\ref{lem:separated-fibres} gives the
contractive uniform tracial approximation assertion.

label: lem:uniform-storage
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:uniform-storage}
Let $A$ be unital, $\mathrm{T}(A)\ne\varnothing$, and suppose positive elements
satisfy simultaneous comparison
\[
 [\mathrm{d}_\tau(a)<\mathrm{d}_\tau(b)\text{ for all }\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)]
 \ \Longrightarrow\ a\precsim b\qquad(a,b\in A_+).
\]
Suppose $a_i\in A_+$, $\left\|a_i\right\|\le2$, and $k_i,\ell_i\in A_+$ are
contractions such that
\[
 \ell_i a_i=a_i,\qquad \ell_i k_i=\ell_i,\qquad
 \mathrm{d}_\tau(k_i)\le\alpha_i\quad(\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)),
 \qquad \sum_{i\ge1}\alpha_i<\tfrac14.
\]
For arbitrary numbers $0<\rho_i\le1$, there exist $H,B\in A_\mathrm{sa}$ and
$D_i\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,H,B)$ such that
\[
 \left\|D_i^*D_i-a_i\right\|<\rho_i\qquad(i\ge1).
\]
Equivalently, the $a_i$ have positive approximants in
$\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,H+iB)$ with the prescribed accuracies.

label: eq:weight-tail-budget
title: Proof
body_md:
Put $R=2$ and $\eta_i=\rho_i/[4(2R+1)]$. We recursively choose positive
numbers $w_i,\mu_i,\lambda_i,\delta_i$ and elements $r_i,e_i\in A$.
Here $e_i$ will be a positive contraction. At stage $i$, choose
$w_i\le2^{-i}$ so small that, for every $j<i$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-tail-budget}
 w_i<2^{-(i-j)}w_j\eta_j/(6R).
\end{equation}
Next choose $\mu_i\le2^{-i}$ so small that, for every $j<i$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:clock-tail-budget}
 2\mu_i<2^{-(i-j)}\lambda_j\eta_j/(6R).
\end{equation}
After $w_i,\mu_i$ have been fixed, choose $0<\lambda_i\le\mu_i$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:past-leak-budget}
 R\sqrt{\frac{3\lambda_i}{\mu_i}}
 +\frac{R}{w_i}\sum_{j<i}w_j
 \left(\sqrt{\frac{3\lambda_i}{\lambda_j}}
       +\sqrt{\frac{3\lambda_i}{\mu_j}}\right)
 <\frac{\eta_i}{3}.
\end{equation}
This is possible because the sum is finite and its left side tends to
zero with $\lambda_i$. Finally choose
\begin{equation}\label{eq:range-band-budget}
 0<\delta_i<\lambda_i\eta_i/(6R).
\end{equation}
These choices only involve data from the preceding stages.

For the comparison step put
\[
 S_i=\sum_{j<i}(\lambda_j e_j+\mu_j k_j)+\mu_i k_i,
 \qquad b_i=(1-S_i/\delta_i)_+.
\]
The support trace of a finite sum of positive elements is at most the
sum of their support traces. Assuming the inductive bounds
$\mathrm{d}_\tau(e_j)\le\alpha_j$, we obtain
\[
 \mathrm{d}_\tau(S_i)\le\sum_{j<i}\alpha_j+\sum_{j\le i}\alpha_j
 <\tfrac12.
\]
As $b_i$ is one on the kernel of $S_i$ in every tracial GNS closure,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:full-complement}
 \mathrm{d}_\tau(b_i)\ge1-\mathrm{d}_\tau(S_i)>\tfrac12
 >\alpha_i\ge \mathrm{d}_\tau(a_i)\qquad(\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)).
\end{equation}
The last inequality follows from $\ell_i a_i=a_i$ and
$\ell_i k_i=\ell_i$: in $A^{**}$ these identities give
\[
 s(a_i)\leq1_{\{1\}}(\ell_i)\leq s(\ell_i)
 \leq1_{\{1\}}(k_i)\leq s(k_i).
\]
Thus $\mathrm{d}_\tau(a_i)\leq\mathrm{d}_\tau(\ell_i)
\leq\mathrm{d}_\tau(k_i)\leq\alpha_i$.
Comparison and Lemma~\ref{lem:unstabilize} give
$v_i\in A$ with
\[
 \left\|v_i^*b_i v_i-a_i\right\|<\rho_i/4.
\]
Set $r_i^0=b_i^{1/2}v_i\ell_i$. Then
\[
 r_i^0 k_i=r_i^0,\qquad
 \left\|(r_i^0)^*r_i^0-a_i\right\|<\rho_i/4,\qquad
 \left\|r_i^0\right\|<R.
\]
Furthermore $(r_i^0)^*r_i^0\in\overline{\ell_i A\ell_i}$, so
\[
 \mathrm{d}_\tau(r_i^0(r_i^0)^*)=\mathrm{d}_\tau((r_i^0)^*r_i^0)
 \le \mathrm{d}_\tau(\ell_i)\le\alpha_i.
\]

Write $h_i=r_i^0(r_i^0)^*\in\overline{b_i A b_i}$. Choose continuous
functions $\chi_i,\gamma_i:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$, both zero near zero,
such that $\gamma_i\chi_i=\chi_i$ and
\[
 \sup_{t\ge0}t(1-\chi_i(t)^2)<\rho_i/4.
\]
Such functions are obtained by making $\chi_i$ equal to one above a
sufficiently small positive threshold, and $\gamma_i$ equal to one on
its support. Put $r_i=\chi_i(h_i)r_i^0$ and $e_i=\gamma_i(h_i)$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-witness-properties}
 \begin{gathered}
 e_i r_i=r_i,\qquad r_i k_i=r_i,\qquad \left\|r_i\right\|<R,\qquad
 \mathrm{d}_\tau(e_i)\le\alpha_i,\\
 \left\|r_i^*r_i-a_i\right\|<\rho_i/2.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The Gram estimate follows from
$(r_i^0)^*\chi_i(h_i)^2r_i^0
=t\chi_i(t)^2|_{t=(r_i^0)^*r_i^0}$.
The range of $r_i$ is contained in the support of $b_i$, which lies
in $1_{[0,\delta_i)}(S_i)$ in $A^{**}$. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:range-eigenvector}
 \left\|S_i r_i\right\|\le\delta_i R.
\end{equation}
This completes the inductive stage.

Define the norm-convergent self-adjoint series
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-clock-payload}
 H=\sum_{i\ge1}(\lambda_i e_i+\mu_i k_i),\qquad
 B=\sum_{i\ge1}w_i(r_i+r_i^*).
\end{equation}
The recursive bounds imply, for each $i$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-tails}
 \sum_{j>i}w_j\le w_i\eta_i/(6R),\qquad
 \sum_{j>i}(\lambda_j+\mu_j)\le\lambda_i\eta_i/(6R).
\end{equation}
Indeed, apply \eqref{eq:weight-tail-budget} with the earlier index $i$
and sum the geometric factors $2^{-(j-i)}$. For the second inequality,
use $\lambda_j+\mu_j\le2\mu_j$ and
\eqref{eq:clock-tail-budget} in the same way.

Let $\chi:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ be continuous, one on $[0,2]$ and zero
on $[3,\infty)$, and put $F_i=\chi(H/\lambda_i)$. The function
\[
 \theta_i(t)=\frac{1-\chi(t/\lambda_i)}{t-\lambda_i},
\]
continued by zero near $\lambda_i$, has norm at most $1/\lambda_i$.
Since
\[
 (1-F_i)r_i=\theta_i(H)(H-\lambda_i)r_i,
\]
\eqref{eq:range-eigenvector} and \eqref{eq:uniform-tails} give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-witness-recovery}
 \left\|F_i r_i-r_i\right\|
 \le\frac{R}{\lambda_i}
 \left(\delta_i+\sum_{j>i}(\lambda_j+\mu_j)\right)
 <\eta_i/3.
\end{equation}
Here we used $e_i r_i=r_i$ to write
$(H-\lambda_i)r_i=S_i r_i+
\sum_{j>i}(\lambda_j e_j+\mu_j k_j)r_i$.

Let $p_j$ and $q_j$ be the left and right support projections of
$r_j$ in $A^{**}$. Since $e_j$ is a positive contraction and $e_jr_j=r_j$, the range
of $r_j$ lies in its eigenvalue-one spectral subspace. Thus
$e_j\ge p_j$. Applying the same argument to $r_jk_j=r_j$ gives
$k_j\ge q_j$. Positivity of $H$ consequently gives
$H\ge\lambda_j p_j$ and $H\ge\mu_j q_j$.
Since $F_i H F_i\le3\lambda_i1$, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-support-leak}
 \left\|F_i r_j\right\|\le R\sqrt{3\lambda_i/\lambda_j},\qquad
 \left\|F_i r_j^*\right\|\le R\sqrt{3\lambda_i/\mu_j}.
\end{equation}
For example,
$F_i p_j F_i\le\lambda_j^{-1}F_i H F_i$
implies $\left\|F_i p_j\right\|\le\sqrt{3\lambda_i/\lambda_j}$.
No commutation of $H$ with the masks or witnesses is asserted.

Set $D_i=w_i^{-1}F_i B\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,H,B)$. Splitting its defining series
into the main term, the own adjoint, the earlier terms and the later
terms, we have
\begin{align*}
 \left\|D_i-r_i\right\|
 &\le\left\|F_i r_i-r_i\right\|+R\sqrt{3\lambda_i/\mu_i}\\
 &\quad+\frac{R}{w_i}\sum_{j<i}w_j
 \left(\sqrt{3\lambda_i/\lambda_j}
       +\sqrt{3\lambda_i/\mu_j}\right)
 +\frac{2R}{w_i}\sum_{j>i}w_j
 <\eta_i.
\end{align*}
The three groups are bounded by \eqref{eq:main-witness-recovery},
\eqref{eq:past-leak-budget}, and \eqref{eq:uniform-tails}, respectively.
Finally $\eta_i\le1$ gives
\[
 \left\|D_i^*D_i-r_i^*r_i\right\|
 \le(2R+\eta_i)\eta_i\le(2R+1)\eta_i=\rho_i/4.
\]
Together with \eqref{eq:uniform-witness-properties}, this proves the
required estimate.

label: thm:uniform-encoding
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:uniform-encoding}
Let $A$ be separable and unital with $\mathrm{T}(A)\ne\varnothing$, and suppose
simultaneous comparison \eqref{eq:comparison} holds. Suppose
$g\in A$ and $C=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g)$ have the following approximation property:
every self-adjoint contraction $z\in A$ can be approximated arbitrarily
well in $\left\|\cdot\right\|_{2,u}$ by self-adjoint contractions in $C$.
Then there is $G\in A$ such that $A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g,G)$.
Replacing $g$ by a scalar shift gives $A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(g,G)$ without
adjoining the unit separately.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $(z_j)$ norm dense in the self-adjoint unit ball of $A$, put
$\varepsilon_k=2^{-k}$, and fix a bijection
$i=i(j,k,\pm)$ between $\mathbb N\times\mathbb N\times\{+,-\}$ and $\mathbb N$.
Set $\alpha_i=2^{-i-5}$. For each $(j,k)$ choose a self-adjoint
contraction $c_{jk}\in C$ with
\[
 \left\|z_j-c_{jk}\right\|_{2,u}^2
 <\tfrac14\varepsilon_k^2\min\{\alpha_{i(j,k,+)},
                                      \alpha_{i(j,k,-)}\}.
\]
For $i=i(j,k,\pm)$ put $t_i=\pm(z_j-c_{jk})$ and
$a_i=(t_i-\varepsilon_k)_+$.
Choose continuous scalar functions $f_k,l_k:\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ such
that $f_k$ is zero below $\varepsilon_k/2$ and one above
$3\varepsilon_k/4$, while $l_k$ is zero below $3\varepsilon_k/4$
and one above $\varepsilon_k$. Set
$k_i=f_k(t_i)$ and $\ell_i=l_k(t_i)$. Thus
$\ell_i a_i=a_i$ and $\ell_i k_i=\ell_i$.
The spectral Markov estimate gives, for every trace,
\[
 \mathrm{d}_\tau(k_i)\le4\varepsilon_k^{-2}
                    \left\|z_j-c_{jk}\right\|_{2,u}^2<\alpha_i.
\]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-storage} with $\rho_i=\varepsilon_k$.
Let $H,B,D_i$ be its outputs and set $G=H+iB$. Since
$H=\operatorname{Re}(G)$ and $B=\operatorname{Im}(G)$, all $D_i$ belong to $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,G)$.
Consequently
\[
 c_{jk}+D_{i(j,k,+)}^*D_{i(j,k,+)}
       -D_{i(j,k,-)}^*D_{i(j,k,-)}\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g,G).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:markov} and the storage estimates, its distance
from $z_j$ is less than $3\varepsilon_k$. Letting $k$ tend to infinity
and using norm density proves $A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g,G)$.
To recover the actual unit under the nonunital generation convention,
replace $g$ by $g+s1$ with $s>\left\|\operatorname{Re}(g)\right\|+1$. Its real part is
positive invertible, so continuous functional calculus gives $1$ in
the generated algebra. The unital subalgebra $C$ is unchanged.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The positive complement $b_i$ is large at every trace, including a
matrix trace where the corresponding error $a_i$ vanishes. Thus every
comparison in the proof is strict at every trace. The positive cutoffs
$e_i,k_i$ may vanish at individual traces.
Only approximate recovery of the witnesses is needed, and its error
is explicitly controlled before the witnesses are chosen. The proof
therefore also includes the joint trace kernel of $A$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lem:bauer-pair} gives $x,y\in A_\mathrm{sa}$ such that
$C=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,x,y)$ has the contractive uniform tracial approximation
property. Put $g=x+iy$, so $C=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g)$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform-encoding}, using \eqref{eq:comparison},
gives $G\in A$ with $A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g,G)$. Its final scalar shift
of $g$ gives $A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(g,G)$ with our generation convention.

label: gr:lem:rounding
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:lem:rounding}
Let $p$ be a projection in $\mathcal M_X$, and write
\[
 H=\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jz_j\in(p\mathcal M_Xp)_\mathrm{sa},
 \qquad \sum_{j=1}^m z_j=p,
\]
where the $z_j$ are orthogonal projections and the real labels
$\lambda_j$ are distinct.  Let $t\in(p\mathcal M_Xp)_\mathrm{sa}$ have
finite spectrum in this corner.  At each spectral value $s$ of $t$,
choose a nearest label $g(s)\in\{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m\}$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{gr:eq:rounding}
 \left\|g(t)-H\right\|_{2,\tau}\leq2\left\|t-H\right\|_{2,\tau}
 \quad(\tau\in X),\qquad
 \left\|g(t)-H\right\|_{2,X}\leq2\left\|t-H\right\|_{2,X}.
\end{equation}
No commutation between $t$ and $H$ is required.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The assertion is trivial if $p=0$.  Otherwise write
$t=\sum_s s q_s$, with an orthogonal spectral partition of $p$.
For every $\tau\in X$, the numbers
\[
 \tau(q_sz_j)=\tau(z_jq_sz_j)
\]
are nonnegative.  Expanding the squares and using the trace property
gives the exact identities
\[
 \left\|g(t)-H\right\|_{2,\tau}^2
 =\sum_{s,j}|g(s)-\lambda_j|^2\tau(q_sz_j),
 \qquad
 \left\|t-H\right\|_{2,\tau}^2
 =\sum_{s,j}|s-\lambda_j|^2\tau(q_sz_j).
\]
Because $g(s)$ is a nearest label,
\[
 |g(s)-\lambda_j|
 \leq |g(s)-s|+|s-\lambda_j|
 \leq2|s-\lambda_j|.
\]
Comparison of the finite sums proves the pointwise inequality in
\eqref{gr:eq:rounding}; taking the supremum proves its uniform
version.  This proof requires neither faithfulness nor normalization
of the traces restricted to the corner.

label: gr:label-transfer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:label-transfer}
Let $p_1,\ldots,p_L$ be orthogonal projections in $A$ summing to
$1$, and put $a_0=\sum_\ell\alpha_\ell p_\ell$.  Fix a nonempty
finite set $\Lambda_\ell\subseteq\mathbb R$ for each $\ell$.
Suppose $H\in(\mathcal M_X)_\mathrm{sa}$ has a presentation
\[
 H=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}
       \lambda z_{\ell,\lambda},\qquad
 \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}z_{\ell,\lambda}=p_\ell,
\]
where the $z_{\ell,\lambda}$ are orthogonal projections in the
completion.  For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are orthogonal
projections $q_{\ell,\lambda}\in p_\ell Ap_\ell$, summing to
$p_\ell$ for each $\ell$, such that
\[
 h=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}
       \lambda q_{\ell,\lambda},\qquad
 \left\|h-H\right\|_{2,X}<\varepsilon.
\]
Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{gr:eq:transfer-norms}
 \left\|h-a_0\right\|\leq
       \max_{\ell,\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}|\lambda-\alpha_\ell|,
 \qquad
 \left\|h\right\|\leq\max_{\ell,\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}|\lambda|.
\end{equation}
The number of spectral values of $h$ is at most
$\sum_\ell|\Lambda_\ell|$.  Neither the label sets nor this bound
depends on $\varepsilon$.  If all the labels are nonzero, $h$ is
invertible in $A$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $H_\ell=p_\ell Hp_\ell$.  First consider a corner whose
canonical image in $\mathcal M_X$ is nonzero.  Bounded uniform
$2$-norm approximation, compression by $p_\ell$, and
symmetrization approximate $H_\ell$ by self-adjoint elements of
$p_\ell Ap_\ell$.  Real rank zero passes to this projection corner
\cite{BrownPedersen},
so each such approximant can in turn be approximated in norm by a
finite-spectrum self-adjoint element.  Thus choose
$t_\ell\in(p_\ell Ap_\ell)_\mathrm{sa}$ of finite spectrum with
\[
 \left\|t_\ell-H_\ell\right\|_{2,X}
 <\frac{\varepsilon}{4\sqrt L}.
\]
Its canonical image still has finite spectrum.  Round each spectral
value of $t_\ell$ in the unital corner $p_\ell Ap_\ell$ to a
nearest member of $\Lambda_\ell$.  The resulting functional-calculus
element has the form
\[
 h_\ell=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}
          \lambda q_{\ell,\lambda},\qquad
 \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell}q_{\ell,\lambda}=p_\ell.
\]
Unused labels have zero projections.  Lemma~\ref{gr:lem:rounding},
applied to the canonical image of $t_\ell$, gives
\[
 \left\|h_\ell-H_\ell\right\|_{2,X}
 <\frac{\varepsilon}{2\sqrt L}.
\]
If the canonical image of $p_\ell$ is zero, assign all of
$p_\ell$ to any one label of $\Lambda_\ell$ and set the other
projections to zero.  This corner contributes zero uniform
$2$-norm error; the same convention covers $p_\ell=0$.

Set $h=\sum_\ell h_\ell$.  Errors from different corners have
zero products, so for every $\tau\in X$,
\[
 \left\|h-H\right\|_{2,\tau}^2
 =\sum_\ell\left\|h_\ell-H_\ell\right\|_{2,\tau}^2
 <\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}.
\]
Taking the supremum gives
$\left\|h-H\right\|_{2,X}\leq\varepsilon/2<\varepsilon$.
All $q_{\ell,\lambda}$ are mutually orthogonal in $A$ and their
sum is $1$.  Applying this decomposition to $h$ and $h-a_0$ gives
\eqref{gr:eq:transfer-norms} and the claimed bound on spectral
values.  When all labels are nonzero, the same decomposition gives
the inverse explicitly:
\[
 h^{-1}=\sum_{\ell,\lambda}\lambda^{-1}q_{\ell,\lambda}.
\]
head: environment

label: gr:positive-interpolation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:positive-interpolation}
Let $A$ be a separable unital $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebra of real rank zero, and suppose
$\mathrm{T}(A)\ne\varnothing$.  There is a norm-dense $G_\delta$ set
$\mathcal S\subseteq A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ such that, whenever
$b\in\mathcal S$, $0\leq a\leq1$, and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a
continuous function $f\colon\mathbb R\to[0,1]$ satisfying
\[
 \sup_{\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)}|\tau(f(b))-\tau(a)|<\varepsilon.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a norm-dense sequence $(a_m)_{m\geq1}$ in the positive unit ball
of $A$.  For $m,k\geq1$, let
\[
 \mathcal U_{m,k}=
 \left\{b\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}:\
 \begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is }f\in \mathrm{C}(\mathbb R,[0,1])\text{ with}\\[-2pt]
 \displaystyle\sup_{\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)}
       |\tau(f(b))-\tau(a_m)|<1/k
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
For a fixed $f$, continuous functional calculus is norm continuous on
bounded sets of self-adjoint elements.  Since every tracial state has
norm one, the strict inequality defining the corresponding subset is
open.  Thus $\mathcal U_{m,k}$ is open.

To see density, choose a finite-spectrum self-adjoint element
$c=\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_jp_j$ in any prescribed nonempty norm-open set.
Here the $\lambda_j$ are distinct and the $p_j$ form an orthogonal
projection partition of $1$.  Put
\[
 d=\sum_{j=1}^s p_j a_m p_j.
\]
Then $0\leq d\leq1$, $cd=dc$, and
$\tau(d)=\tau(a_m)$ for every $\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)$.  Choose $t>0$ small
enough that $b=c+td$ remains in the prescribed open set and the
intervals $[\lambda_j,\lambda_j+t]$ are pairwise disjoint.  There is
$f\in \mathrm{C}(\mathbb R,[0,1])$ with
\[
 f(\lambda_j+tu)=u\qquad(0\leq u\leq1, 1\leq j\leq s).
\]
Functional calculus in each $p_j$-corner gives $f(b)=d$.  In particular,
$b\in\mathcal U_{m,k}$.  Baire's theorem now shows that
$\mathcal S=\bigcap_{m,k}\mathcal U_{m,k}$ is a dense $G_\delta$.
Approximating an arbitrary positive contraction by $a_m$ proves the
claimed interpolation property.
head: environment

label: gr:clopen-recovery
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:clopen-recovery}
Let $A$ and $\mathcal S$ be as in
Lemma~\ref{gr:positive-interpolation}, let $b\in\mathcal S$, and let
$K_0\subseteq\partial\mathrm{T}(A)$ be nonempty and compact.  For every
clopen $V\subseteq K_0$, the central projection
$z=1_V\in \mathrm{C}(K_0)\subseteq\mathcal M_{K_0}$ is a uniform $2$-norm
limit of positive contractions in $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,b)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose a positive contraction $a\in A$ with
$\|a-z\|_{2,K_0}<\varepsilon^2/2$.  Thus
$|\tau(a)-1_V(\tau)|<\varepsilon^2/2$ for $\tau\in K_0$.
Lemma~\ref{gr:positive-interpolation} gives a positive contraction
$d=f(b)\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,b)$ with
\[
 |\tau(d)-1_V(\tau)|<\varepsilon^2\qquad(\tau\in K_0).
\]
In each such fiber, $z$ is either $0$ or $1$.  The inequalities
$d^2\leq d$ and $(1-d)^2\leq1-d$ consequently give
\[
 \|d-z\|_{2,\tau}^2
 \leq|\tau(d)-1_V(\tau)|<\varepsilon^2.
\]
Since $K_0$ is compact, the continuous strict error has a maximum
strictly below $\varepsilon^2$.  Taking $\varepsilon\downarrow0$
gives the conclusion.
head: environment

label: gr:local-witnesses
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:local-witnesses}
Let $K_0\subseteq\partial\mathrm{T}(A)$ be nonempty and compact, let
$b\in\mathcal S$, and put $B=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,h,b)$ for $h\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$.
Suppose $K_0=V_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup V_s$ is a finite clopen
partition and $x\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$, $c_i\in B_{\mathrm{sa}}$ satisfy
\[
 \max_i\|x-c_i\|_{2,V_i}<\varepsilon.
\]
For every $\zeta>0$, a self-adjoint noncommutative polynomial $F$
then satisfies
$\|x-F(h,b)\|_{2,K_0}<\varepsilon+\zeta$.
Constant terms are allowed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The claim is immediate for $x=0$, so assume $R_0=\|x\|>0$.
Clipping the $c_i$ to $[-R_0,R_0]$ does not increase any error,
by~\eqref{gr:clipping}.  We may therefore assume $\|c_i\|\leq R_0$.
With $z_i=1_{V_i}$, set
\[
 C=\sum_i z_i c_i\in\mathcal M_{K_0}.
\]
The $z_i$ are central orthogonal projections summing to $1$, so
$C=C^*$, $\|C\|\leq R_0$, and $\|x-C\|_{2,K_0}<\varepsilon$.
Choose positive contractions $d_{i,n}\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,b)$ converging
uniformly in $2$-norm to $z_i$, by Lemma~\ref{gr:clopen-recovery}.
Then
\[
 D_n=\frac12\sum_i(d_{i,n}c_i+c_i d_{i,n})\in B_{\mathrm{sa}}
\]
converges uniformly in $2$-norm to $C$, because multiplication by
$c_i$ increases each error by at most $R_0$.  Clipping $D_n$ to
$[-R_0,R_0]$ gives bounded self-adjoint elements $v_n\in B$ that
still converge to $C$.  Approximate a sufficiently late $v_n$ in
norm by a self-adjoint polynomial in $h,b$, and choose the two
approximation errors to have sum less than $\zeta$.
head: environment

label: gr:fixed-label-approximation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{gr:fixed-label-approximation}
Let $A$ be separable, unital, and of real rank
zero, and suppose $K=\partial\mathrm{T}(A)$ is nonempty, compact, and
zero-dimensional.  Fix
\[
 a_0=\sum_{\ell=1}^L\alpha_\ell p_\ell\in A_{\mathrm{sa}},
\]
where the $\alpha_\ell$ are distinct and the $p_\ell$ form a nonzero
orthogonal projection partition of $1$.  Fix also
$b_0\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ and $\eta>0$.
There are pairwise disjoint finite sets of nonzero real labels
$\Lambda_\ell$, with total cardinality $R$, such that for every
$x\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ and $\delta>0$ there are $h,b\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$
and a self-adjoint polynomial $F$ satisfying
\[
 \|h-a_0\|<\eta,\qquad \|b-b_0\|<\eta,\qquad
 \|x-F(h,b)\|_{2,\mathrm{T}(A)}<\delta.
\]
Moreover, $b\in\mathcal S$, and $h$ is invertible, with a spectral
decomposition using labels in $\Lambda_\ell$ on subprojections of
$p_\ell$.  In particular, $h$ has at most $R$ spectral values.
The sets $\Lambda_\ell$ and $R$ depend only on $a_0,b_0,\eta$, and
are independent of $x$ and $\delta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{gr:common-labels} with the scalar labels
$\alpha_\ell$, norm bound $\|b_0\|$, and norm tolerance $\eta/8$.
This fixes the sets $\Lambda_\ell$ and their total cardinality $R$.
At each $\tau\in K$, the lemma gives $H_\tau,B_\tau\in(M_\tau)_{\mathrm{sa}}$
with
\[
 \ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(H_\tau,B_\tau)=M_\tau,\qquad
 \|H_\tau-\pi_\tau(a_0)\|<\eta/8,\qquad
 \|B_\tau-\pi_\tau(b_0)\|<\eta/8.
\]
The spectral projections of $H_\tau$ with labels in
$\Lambda_\ell$ sum to $\pi_\tau(p_\ell)$.  Some may vanish.
The same assertion applies to matrix and scalar factors.

Only now fix $x$ and $\delta$.  The Kaplansky density theorem and polynomial
approximation give a self-adjoint polynomial $P_\tau$ with
\[
 \|\pi_\tau(x)-P_\tau(H_\tau,B_\tau)\|_{2,\tau}<\delta/16.
\]
Lemma~\ref{gr:label-transfer}, applied at the singleton $\{\tau\}$,
approximates $H_\tau$ arbitrarily closely in $2$-norm by
$h_\tau\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ with the prescribed labels refining
the $p_\ell$.  Thus $\|h_\tau-a_0\|<\eta/8$.
Apply the Kaplansky density theorem to obtain bounded self-adjoint
approximants to $B_\tau-\pi_\tau(b_0)$. The norm-controlled quotient
lifting of Lemma~\ref{lem:lift} then gives $b_\tau\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ with
$\|b_\tau-b_0\|<\eta/4$, and image arbitrarily close to $B_\tau$
in $2$-norm.  Norm-bounded polynomial $2$-norm continuity allows
these approximations to be chosen so that
\[
 \|x-P_\tau(h_\tau,b_\tau)\|_{2,\tau}<\delta/8.
\]
For these fixed elements and polynomial, the squared error is
continuous in the trace.  It is consequently less than
$(\delta/4)^2$ on an open neighborhood of $\tau$ in $K$.

Choose a finite disjoint clopen partition
$K=V_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup V_s$ subordinate to these neighborhoods.
Write $h_i,b_i,P_i$ for the corresponding choices.  Compactness
of each $V_i$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{gr:local-errors}
 \max_i\|x-P_i(h_i,b_i)\|_{2,V_i}<\delta/4.
\end{equation}
In $\mathcal M_K$, put
\[
 \widetilde H=\sum_i z_i h_i,\qquad
 \widetilde B=\sum_i z_i b_i,\qquad z_i=1_{V_i}.
\]
Central orthogonality gives
$\|\widetilde H-a_0\|<\eta/8$ and
$\|\widetilde B-b_0\|<\eta/4$.
The first element still has the prescribed label decomposition:
if $q_{i,\ell,\lambda}$ are the spectral projections of $h_i$ in
$p_\ell A p_\ell$, then
$\sum_i z_iq_{i,\ell,\lambda}$ are orthogonal projections, with
sum $p_\ell$ over $\lambda\in\Lambda_\ell$.

Apply Lemma~\ref{gr:label-transfer} over $K$ to approximate
$\widetilde H$ arbitrarily closely in uniform $2$-norm by $h\in A$
with the same labels and $\|h-a_0\|<\eta/8$.
Bounded approximation of $\widetilde B-b_0$ gives
$b_1\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ with $\|b_1-b_0\|<\eta/2$ and
arbitrarily small uniform $2$-norm distance from $\widetilde B$.
There are only finitely many $P_i$, and all coordinates are
uniformly norm bounded.  The approximations can therefore be
chosen, using~\eqref{gr:local-errors}, so that
\[
 \max_i\|x-P_i(h,b_1)\|_{2,V_i}<\delta/2.
\]
These strict inequalities persist under a sufficiently small norm
perturbation of $b_1$.  By density of $\mathcal S$, choose such a
perturbation $b\in\mathcal S$ with $\|b-b_0\|<\eta$.
Lemma~\ref{gr:local-witnesses}, with $c_i=P_i(h,b)$, error
$\delta/2$, and additional tolerance $\delta/2$, produces $F$ with
$\|x-F(h,b)\|_{2,K}<\delta$.  The supremum of the continuous
affine squared error over $\mathrm{T}(A)$ equals its supremum over $K$.
Finally, the spectrum of $h$ is contained in the predetermined
nonzero label set, proving invertibility and the stated bound.

The local polynomials, partition, and transfer accuracies may
depend on $x$ and $\delta$.  The label sets and their cardinality
were fixed before either was chosen.  The final pair need not
weakly generate all fibers simultaneously; only the displayed
uniform approximation is used.
head: environment

label: gr:small-support
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:small-support}
Let $A$ be a unital $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebra of real rank zero, and let
$\varnothing\ne X\subseteq \mathrm{T}(A)$.  Given $\kappa,\eta>0$, there exists
$\delta>0$ such that every $d=d^*\in A$ satisfying
$\|d\|_{2,X}<\delta$ admits a projection $c\in A$ and an element
$y=y^*\in cAc$ with
\[
  \sup_{\tau\in X}\tau(c)<\kappa,
  \qquad \|d-y\|<\eta.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $\alpha,\delta>0$ such that
$\alpha+\delta<\eta$ and $4\delta^2/\alpha^2<\kappa$.
By real rank zero, choose a finite-spectrum self-adjoint element $k\in A$
with $\|d-k\|<\delta$.  Set
\[
  c=1_{\{t:\,|t|>\alpha\}}(k),\qquad y=kc.
\]
The finiteness of the spectrum of $k$ ensures that $c$ is a projection
in $A$.  Also $y=y^*\in cAc$, and
\[
  \|d-y\|\le \|d-k\|+\|k(1-c)\|
  <\delta+\alpha<\eta.
\]
The spectral inequality $\alpha^2c\le k^2$ gives, for every $\tau\in X$,
\[
  \tau(c)\le \alpha^{-2}\tau(k^2)
  \le \alpha^{-2}\|k\|_{2,X}^2
  <\frac{4\delta^2}{\alpha^2}<\kappa.
\]
Here $\|k\|_{2,X}\le\|d\|_{2,X}+\|k-d\|<2\delta$.
The same fixed upper bound applies to the supremum over $X$.
head: environment

label: gr:uniform-norm-encoding
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:uniform-norm-encoding}
Let $A$ be a unital $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebra of real rank zero with
$\mathrm{T}(A)\ne\varnothing$.  Suppose that projections in $A$ satisfy
\[
  \bigl[\tau(p)<\tau(q)\text{ for every }\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)\bigr]
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad p\precsim q.
\]
Here $\precsim$ denotes Murray--von Neumann subequivalence when its
arguments are projections.  Let
\[
  h=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\lambda_jp_j\in A_{\mathrm{sa}},
  \qquad b\in A_{\mathrm{sa}},
\]
where the $p_j$ are nonzero orthogonal projections summing to $1$, and
the labels $\lambda_j$ are distinct and nonzero.  Suppose that a projection
$c\in A$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
  r(r+2)\tau(c)<1\qquad(\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)).
  \label{gr:encoding-capacity}
\end{equation}
For every $y=y^*\in cAc$ and every $\rho,\nu>0$, there exist
$h',b'\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ such that
\[
  \|h'-h\|<\rho,\qquad \|b'-b\|<\rho,
  \qquad \operatorname{dist}\bigl(y,\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h',b')\bigr)<\nu.
\]
Moreover, $h'$ is invertible and $h\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h',b')$.
head: environment

label: gr:compression-error
title: Proof
body_md:
We first compress $y$ into a projection commuting with $h$.
Hereditary subalgebras of a real-rank-zero algebra have approximate
identities consisting of projections; see \cite{BrownPedersen}.
For each $j$, choose a projection
$Q_j\in\operatorname{Her}(p_jcp_j)$ so that, with $Q=\sum_jQ_j$,
\begin{equation}
  d:=QyQ\quad\text{satisfies}\quad\|y-d\|<\nu.
  \label{gr:compression-error}
\end{equation}
Indeed, a projection approximate identity in
$\operatorname{Her}(p_jcp_j)$ satisfies
\[
  \|(p_j-Q_j)c\|^2
  =\|(p_j-Q_j)(p_jcp_j)(p_j-Q_j)\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
As there are only finitely many $j$, this gives
$\|(1-Q)c\|\longrightarrow0$.  Since $y=cyc$,
\[
  \|y-QyQ\|\le2\|y\|\,\|(1-Q)c\|,
\]
which proves the required choice.  If $Q=0$, then $\|y\|<\nu$ and
we may take $h'=h$, $b'=b$.  The original $h$ is invertible, so all
conclusions hold in this case.  We henceforth assume $Q\ne0$.

Each $Q_j$ is Murray--von Neumann subequivalent to $c$.
To see this, a projection in $\operatorname{Her}(p_jcp_j)$ is Cuntz
subequivalent to $p_jcp_j$, and $p_jcp_j$ is Cuntz subequivalent to $c$.
For projections, Cuntz subequivalence agrees with Murray--von Neumann
subequivalence.  Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \tau(Q)=\sum_j\tau(Q_j)\le r\tau(c)
  \qquad(\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)).
  \label{gr:Q-trace}
\end{equation}

We next construct a buffer projection containing $Q$.  Put
\[
  z_j=(p_j-Q_j)bQ.
\]
Choose a projection $f_j\in\operatorname{Her}(z_jz_j^*)$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
  \|(p_j-Q_j-f_j)z_j\|<\frac{\rho}{4r}.
  \label{gr:buffer-corner-error}
\end{equation}
A projection approximate identity for $\operatorname{Her}(z_jz_j^*)$
converges on $z_j$ in norm, so this is possible.  If $z_j=0$, take
$f_j=0$.  In all cases $f_j\le p_j-Q_j$.  Also $f_j\precsim Q$:
indeed, $f_j$ is Cuntz subequivalent to $z_jz_j^*$, this positive element
is Cuntz equivalent to $z_j^*z_j$, and
$0\le z_j^*z_j\le\|b\|^2Q$.

Set
\[
  E_j=Q_j+f_j\le p_j,\qquad E=\sum_jE_j.
\]
Then $E$ is a projection, $Q\le E$, and $Eh=hE$.  Equation
\eqref{gr:buffer-corner-error} gives
\begin{equation}
  \|Qb(1-E)\|=\|(1-E)bQ\|
  \le\sum_j\|(p_j-Q_j-f_j)z_j\|<\rho/4.
  \label{gr:buffer-error}
\end{equation}
Its trace cost does not depend on this accuracy:
\begin{equation}
  \tau(E)\le\tau(Q)+r\tau(Q)=(r+1)\tau(Q).
  \label{gr:buffer-trace}
\end{equation}
Together with \eqref{gr:encoding-capacity} and \eqref{gr:Q-trace}, this
implies
\[
  \tau(Q)+\tau(E)\le(r+2)\tau(Q)
  \le r(r+2)\tau(c)<1\qquad(\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)).
\]
Thus $\tau(Q)<\tau(1-E)$ for every trace.  Projection comparison gives
a projection $P_0\le1-E$ with $P_0\sim Q$.

The projection $P_0$ need not commute with $h$.  We replace it by an
equivalent projection that does.  Real rank zero implies that $V(A)$
is a refinement monoid \cite[Lemma~2.3]{AraPardo}.
Apply finite refinement to
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{j=1}^{r}[Q_j]+[1-E-P_0]
  =[1-E]=\sum_{k=1}^{r}[p_k-E_k].
  \label{gr:refinement-equality}
\end{equation}
This yields actual orthogonal decompositions
\begin{equation}
  Q_j=\sum_{k=1}^{r}Q_{jk},\qquad
  p_k-E_k=\sum_{j=1}^{r}P_{jk}+R_k,
  \qquad Q_{jk}\sim P_{jk},
  \label{gr:refinement-decompositions}
\end{equation}
with zero summands permitted.  We justify the passage from classes to
actual subprojections.  If a projection $q\in A$ satisfies
$[q]=\sum_{\ell}x_{\ell}$ in $V(A)$, choose matrix-projection
representatives of the $x_{\ell}$.  A partial isometry implementing the
equivalence of their direct sum with $q$ transports the summands to
orthogonal subprojections of $q$.  These subprojections belong to the
corner $qAq$.  Apply this separately to every row and column of the
refinement matrix for \eqref{gr:refinement-equality}.  The resulting
matching subprojections have equal classes.  Equivalence of two
projections in $A$, initially implemented in a matrix algebra, is
implemented in $A$ itself: compress the implementing partial isometry
to their initial and final matrix corners.  This proves
\eqref{gr:refinement-decompositions} without cancellation.

Put
\[
  P_k=\sum_jP_{jk},\qquad P=\sum_kP_k.
\]
Then $P\le1-E$, $Ph=hP$, and $P\perp Q$.
Adding partial isometries from $P_{jk}$ to $Q_{jk}$ gives
$w\in QAP$ with
\begin{equation}
  w^*w=P,\qquad ww^*=Q,\qquad wP_{jk}w^*=Q_{jk}.
  \label{gr:transport}
\end{equation}
Orthogonality of the initial and final projections makes the sum a
partial isometry.

Choose $0<\delta_0<\rho/4$ and define
\begin{equation}
  b'=b-QbP-PbQ+\delta_0(w+w^*).
  \label{gr:bridge-coordinate}
\end{equation}
This element is self-adjoint and satisfies $Qb'P=\delta_0w$.  Moreover,
\[
  \|b'-b\|\le2\|QbP\|+2\delta_0
  \le2\|Qb(1-E)\|+2\delta_0<\rho.
\]
It remains to make $Q$, $P$, and the stored element spectrally
recoverable.

Set
\[
  L=\max\{1,\|d\|\},\qquad e=L^{-1}w^*dw\in(PAP)_{\mathrm{sa}}.
\]
Then $\|e\|\le1$ and $d=Lwew^*$.
Choose $s>0$ with $7s<\rho$ so that the intervals
$\lambda_j+[0,7s]$ are pairwise disjoint and avoid zero.
For each fixed $j$, choose distinct numbers $t_{jk}\in(0,s/2)$ for
the nonzero $Q_{jk}$, and define
\begin{equation}
  h'=h+\sum_{j,k}(3s+t_{jk})Q_{jk}+6sP+se,
  \label{gr:storage-coordinate}
\end{equation}
omitting zero summands.  Since $P\perp Q$, we have
$\|h'-h\|\le7s<\rho$.

The projections $P$, $Q_{jk}$, and $1-P-Q$ reduce $h'$.
On $1-P-Q$, the element $h'$ equals $h$; on $Q_{jk}$ it is the scalar
$\lambda_j+3s+t_{jk}$.  In the $P$-corner it is
\[
  Ph'P=\sum_k(\lambda_k+6s)P_k+se.
\]
Although $e$ need not commute with the individual $P_k$, the
self-adjoint spectral perturbation estimate and $\|se\|\le s$ give
\begin{equation}
  \operatorname{sp}_{PAP}(Ph'P)
  \subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^{r}\bigl(\lambda_k+[5s,7s]\bigr).
  \label{gr:storage-spectral-bands}
\end{equation}
The unchanged scalar labels, the individual $Q_{jk}$ labels, and the
union of bands in \eqref{gr:storage-spectral-bands} are mutually
disjoint.  They all avoid zero.  Thus $h'$ is invertible, and
$1\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h')$ even with the convention that a unit is not
automatically adjoined.  Continuous functional calculus recovers every
$Q_{jk}$ and the aggregate projection $P$ from $h'$; it therefore also
recovers $Q=\sum_{j,k}Q_{jk}$.

Let $D=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h',b')$.  Equation \eqref{gr:bridge-coordinate} gives
$w=\delta_0^{-1}Qb'P\in D$.  Then \eqref{gr:transport} gives
\[
  P_{jk}=w^*Q_{jk}w\in D,
  \qquad P_k=\sum_jP_{jk}\in D,
  \qquad hP=\sum_k\lambda_kP_k\in D.
\]
Consequently,
\[
  e=s^{-1}(Ph'P-hP-6sP)\in D,
  \qquad d=Lwew^*\in D.
\]
Equation \eqref{gr:compression-error} proves
$\operatorname{dist}(y,D)<\nu$.  Finally,
\[
  h=h'-\sum_{j,k}(3s+t_{jk})Q_{jk}-6sP-se\in D.
\]
This last recovery uses both coordinates; no assertion that
$h\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h')$ is needed.

The construction also covers scalar auxiliary corners.  In such a
corner a hereditary subalgebra is either zero or the whole corner, and
the projection choices above remain available.  If $A=\mathbb C$,
condition \eqref{gr:encoding-capacity} forces $c=0$, which is the
already handled trivial case.
head: environment

label: gr:capacity-remark
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{gr:capacity-remark}
The capacity bound \eqref{gr:encoding-capacity} depends only on the
number $r$ of spectral values of $h$.  It is independent of $\rho$,
$\nu$, $\|y\|$, and any previously chosen polynomial.  The buffer
projections make \eqref{gr:buffer-error} arbitrarily accurate without
increasing the trace bound \eqref{gr:buffer-trace}.  Normalizing by $L$
then permits an arbitrarily small perturbation of the first coordinate.
In particular, if $r\le R$ is fixed in advance, the uniform bound
\[
  \sup_{\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\tau(c)<\frac{1}{2R(R+2)}
\]
suffices for every subsequent choice of the norm tolerances.
head: environment
name: Capacity and accuracy

label: gr:density-criterion
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{gr:density-criterion}
Let $A$ be a separable $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}$-algebra.  Suppose that for every
$a,b,x\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there are
$a',b'\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ such that
\[
  \|a'-a\|<\varepsilon,\qquad
  \|b'-b\|<\varepsilon,\qquad
  \operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(a',b')\bigr)<\varepsilon.
\]
Then the generating self-adjoint pairs form a norm-dense $G_\delta$
subset of $A_{\mathrm{sa}}^2$, and the single generators form a
norm-dense $G_\delta$ subset of $A$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a dense sequence $(x_j)$ in $A_{\mathrm{sa}}$.  For $j,m\ge1$, set
\[
  U_{j,m}=\bigl\{(a,b)\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}^2:
       \operatorname{dist}(x_j,\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(a,b))<1/m\bigr\}.
\]
These sets are open: a noncommutative polynomial with zero constant
term witnesses a strict inequality, and its evaluation is norm
continuous.  They are dense by hypothesis.  Their intersection is
exactly the set of generating self-adjoint pairs, so the Baire category
theorem proves the first assertion.  The real-linear homeomorphism
$(a,b)\mapsto a+ib$ takes this set to the set of single generators,
because $\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(a+ib)=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(a,b)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $a,b_0,x\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ and $\varepsilon>0$.
We verify Lemma~\ref{gr:density-criterion}.
Put $\eta=\varepsilon/8$.  By real rank zero, choose an invertible
finite-spectrum element $a_0\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ with
$\|a-a_0\|<\eta$.

Apply the fixed-label part of
Proposition~\ref{gr:fixed-label-approximation} to $a_0,b_0$ and the norm tolerance $\eta$.  Its finite set of nonzero labels, and hence a bound $R$
on the number of spectral values of its first coordinate, are fixed
before the target and the required tracial accuracy.  Set
\begin{equation}
  \kappa=\frac{1}{2R(R+2)}.
  \label{gr:main-capacity}
\end{equation}
Use Lemma~\ref{gr:small-support}, with $X=\mathrm{T}(A)$ and norm-error tolerance
$\varepsilon/4$, to choose the corresponding $\delta>0$.

Now apply Proposition~\ref{gr:fixed-label-approximation} with target $x$
and accuracy $\delta$.  It gives $h,b\in A_{\mathrm{sa}}$ and a
self-adjoint noncommutative polynomial $F$ such that
\[
  \|h-a_0\|<\eta,\qquad \|b-b_0\|<\eta,
  \qquad \|x-F(h,b)\|_{2,\mathrm{T}(A)}<\delta,
\]
where
\[
  h=\sum_{j=1}^{r}\lambda_jp_j,\qquad r\le R,
\]
and the $\lambda_j$ are distinct and nonzero while the $p_j$ are
nonzero orthogonal projections summing to $1$.
Lemma~\ref{gr:small-support} gives a projection $c\in A$ and
$y=y^*\in cAc$ with
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{\tau\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\tau(c)<\kappa,
  \qquad \|x-F(h,b)-y\|<\varepsilon/4.
  \label{gr:main-local-error}
\end{equation}
For every trace $\tau$ we therefore have
\[
  r(r+2)\tau(c)\le R(R+2)\tau(c)<1/2<1.
\]

Only now, after $F$ is fixed, choose $0<\rho<\eta$ so that
\[
  \|F(h',b')-F(h,b)\|<\varepsilon/4
\]
whenever $\|h'-h\|,\|b'-b\|<\rho$.
Lemma~\ref{gr:uniform-norm-encoding}, with $\nu=\varepsilon/4$, gives
such a pair $h',b'$, with $h'$ invertible, and an element
$y'\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h',b')$ satisfying $\|y-y'\|<\varepsilon/4$.
Invertibility of $h'$ ensures that $1\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h',b')$.
Thus $F(h',b')$ belongs to this algebra even if $F$ has a constant term.
Consequently,
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{dist}\bigl(x,\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(h',b')\bigr)
  &\le \|x-F(h,b)-y\|
       +\|F(h,b)-F(h',b')\|+\|y-y'\|\\
  &<3\varepsilon/4<\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
Also
\[
  \|h'-a\|<3\eta<\varepsilon,
  \qquad \|b'-b_0\|<2\eta<\varepsilon.
\]
Lemma~\ref{gr:density-criterion} now proves that the generating
self-adjoint pairs and the single generators form norm-dense
$G_\delta$ sets.  The generator-rank characterization for unital
algebras \cite[Theorem~3.4]{ThielGR} yields $\operatorname{gr}(A)\le1$.
If $A$ is noncommutative, it cannot be generated by one self-adjoint
element.  Hence $\operatorname{gr}(A)\ne0$, and
$\operatorname{gr}(A)=1$.
head: environment

label: gr:order-of-choices
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{gr:order-of-choices}
The dependencies in the proof are
\[
  (a_0,b_0,\eta)\ ;\ (R,\kappa,\delta)\ ;\
  (h,b,F)\ ;\ (c,y)\ ;\ (\rho,h',b',y').
\]
The pair $h,b$ is allowed to depend on $x$ and $\delta$.
What is fixed beforehand is the bound $R$ on the spectral complexity
of the first coordinate.  Neither the number of clopen patches nor
the degrees and coefficients of their polynomial witnesses enter
\eqref{gr:main-capacity}.  The norm encoding accommodates every
smaller final perturbation demanded by the polynomial $F$.

label: fg:lem:extraction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:extraction}
Let \(u\) be a unitary with spectrum \(\mathbb T\), and let
\(y=\sum_j\psi_j b_j\psi_j\), where \(b_j=b_j^*\in A\).
For each \(i\geq1\), choose a source set \(S_i\) of at most two labels
and a range label \(\ell_i\) satisfying \eqref{fg:eq:orientation}.
Choose positive contractions \(e_i,\phi_i\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(u)\), supported
in \(J_{\ell_i}\), such that
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:range-cutoffs}
\phi_i e_i^{1/2}=e_i^{1/2},
\qquad
\phi_i e_h^{1/2}=0\quad(h\neq i).
\end{equation}
Suppose
\[
r_i=e_i^{1/2}v_i\kappa_{S_i}\in A,
\qquad \sup_i\left\|r_i\right\|<\infty.
\]
For positive summable coefficients \(\alpha_i\), define
\[
G=\sum_{i=1}^\infty\alpha_i(r_i+r_i^*),\qquad h=y+G.
\]
Then \(G\) converges in norm and
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:extraction}
\phi_i h d_{S_i}=\alpha_i r_i\qquad(i\geq1).
\end{equation}
In particular, \(r_i,G,y\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,u,h)\).
head: environment

label: fg:eq:background-zero
title: Proof
body_md:
The uniform bound on \(r_i\) proves norm convergence. We examine
the three types of terms in the compression.

For the background, \eqref{fg:eq:core-background} makes
\(\phi_i\psi_j=0\) unless \(j=\ell_i\), while
\eqref{fg:eq:far-source} gives \(\psi_{\ell_i}d_{S_i}=0\). Thus
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:background-zero}
\phi_i y d_{S_i}=0.
\end{equation}

For the ordinary witness terms, the disjoint range cutoffs give
\[
\phi_i r_h d_{S_i}=0\quad(h\neq i).
\]
For \(h=i\), \eqref{fg:eq:range-cutoffs} and \eqref{fg:eq:plateau} give
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:own-witness}
\phi_i r_i d_{S_i}=r_i.
\end{equation}

For an adjoint term, write
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:adjoint-expression}
\phi_i r_h^*d_{S_i}
=\phi_i\kappa_{S_h}v_h^*e_h^{1/2}d_{S_i}.
\end{equation}
If \(\ell_h\notin S_i\), the rightmost product is zero by
\eqref{fg:eq:core-source}. If \(\ell_h\in S_i\), the assignment for
witness \(i\) gives \(\ell_i\to\ell_h\).
The membership \(\ell_i\in S_h\) would give the reverse arrow
\(\ell_h\to\ell_i\), which is impossible. Therefore
\(\ell_i\notin S_h\), and the leftmost product in
\eqref{fg:eq:adjoint-expression} is zero. This proves
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:adjoint-zero}
\phi_i r_h^*d_{S_i}=0\qquad\text{for every }h,
\end{equation}
including \(h=i\).

The identities prove \eqref{fg:eq:extraction} for finite sums and then,
by norm convergence, for the series. Both compression factors belong
to \(\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(u)\), so division by the nonzero scalar \(\alpha_i\)
recovers \(r_i\) inside \(\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,u,h)\). The series recovers \(G\),
and subtraction recovers \(y=h-G\).

label: fg:lem:witness
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:witness}
Assume \textup{(C)}. Let \(a,e\in A_+\) and let
\(\kappa\in A_+\) be a contraction such that
\[
\kappa a=a,\qquad
\mathrm{d}_\rho(a)<\mathrm{d}_\rho(e)\quad(\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)).
\]
For every \(\eta>0\) there is \(v\in A\) such that
\[
r=e^{1/2}v\kappa,\qquad
\left\|r^*r-a\right\|<\eta,\qquad
\left\|r\right\|^2\leq\left\|a\right\|+\eta.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Comparison and Lemma~\ref{lem:unstabilize} give \(v\in A\) with
\(\left\|v^*ev-a\right\|<\eta\). Since \(\kappa a=a=a\kappa\),
\[
\left\|r^*r-a\right\|=\left\|\kappa(v^*ev-a)\kappa\right\|<\eta.
\]
The norm bound follows.
head: environment

label: fg:lem:correction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:correction}
Let \(\mathcal B\subseteq A\) satisfy \eqref{fg:eq:uniform-approx}, and
assume \textup{(C)}. Let \(z=z^*\in A\) be a contraction,
\(f\in\mathcal B\) satisfy \(\left\|f\right\|\leq2\), and let
\(\kappa\in\mathcal B_+\) be a contraction with
\(\kappa f=f\kappa=f\). Fix \(0<\varepsilon\leq1/2\) and
positive contractions \(e_+,e_-\in A\) such that
\[
\mu:=\min\left\{
\inf_{\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\mathrm{d}_\rho(e_+),
\inf_{\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\mathrm{d}_\rho(e_-)
\right\}>0.
\]
There are a self-adjoint contraction \(c\in\mathcal B\) and elements
\[
r_\pm=e_\pm^{1/2}v_\pm\kappa\in A,\qquad\left\|r_\pm\right\|\leq3,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:correct-target}
\left\|f^*zf-(f^*cf+r_+^*r_+-r_-^*r_-)\right\|<3\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a self-adjoint contraction \(c\in\mathcal B\) with
\[
\left\|z-c\right\|_{2,\mathrm{T}(A)}<\varepsilon\sqrt\mu/8.
\]
Put \(q=f^*(z-c)f\) and
\(a_\pm=(\pm q-\varepsilon)_+\). Then
\[
\left\|q\right\|\leq8,\qquad
\left\|q\right\|_{2,\mathrm{T}(A)}\leq4\left\|z-c\right\|_{2,\mathrm{T}(A)}
<\varepsilon\sqrt\mu/2.
\]
Equation \eqref{fg:eq:markov} gives, for every \(\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)\),
\[
\mathrm{d}_\rho(a_\pm)<\mu/4<\mathrm{d}_\rho(e_\pm).
\]
The source equations give \(\kappa q=q=q\kappa\), hence
\(\kappa a_\pm=a_\pm\). For the latter assertion, approximate
the functions \((\pm t-\varepsilon)_+\), which vanish at zero,
by polynomials with zero constant term on
\(\sigma(q)\cup\{0\}\).

Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:witness}, with error \(\varepsilon\), supplies
\[
\left\|r_\pm^*r_\pm-a_\pm\right\|<\varepsilon,
\qquad \left\|r_\pm\right\|^2\leq8+\varepsilon<9.
\]
Combining these errors with \eqref{fg:eq:truncation} proves
\eqref{fg:eq:correct-target}. Both signs use the same \(c\).
head: environment

label: fg:eq:targets
title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(\mathcal B=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,u,y)\), and use \eqref{fg:eq:uniform-approx}.
Choose a norm-dense sequence \((z_\nu)\) in the self-adjoint unit
ball of \(A\), and write \(\Omega=\{1,-1,i,-i\}\).
For each tuple
\[
\beta=(\nu,j,k,\zeta,m),\qquad
\nu,m\geq1,\quad 0\leq j,k\leq22,\quad\zeta\in\Omega,
\]
set
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:targets}
f_\beta=\theta_j+\zeta\theta_k,\qquad
S_\beta=\{j,k\},\qquad \varepsilon_\beta=2^{-m}.
\end{equation}
We have \(\left\|f_\beta\right\|\leq2\), and
\(\kappa_{S_\beta}f_\beta=f_\beta\kappa_{S_\beta}=f_\beta\).

Each tuple will use two witnesses, one for each sign. Enumerate the
countable set of pairs \((\beta,\sigma)\), \(\sigma\in\{+,-\}\),
by \(i\geq1\). Assign both signs of \(\beta\) the range label
\(\ell(S_\beta)\) from Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:orientation}.

Within each arc \(J_l\), choose pairwise disjoint open subintervals,
one for each index whose range label is \(l\). Choose in the assigned
subinterval a nonzero continuous positive contraction \(e_i\) and
a continuous positive contraction \(\phi_i\) equal to one on
\(\operatorname{supp} e_i\), with both supports compactly contained in that
subinterval. These choices give \eqref{fg:eq:range-cutoffs}.
Such a countable family of intervals exists, for example by choosing
intervals along a sequence converging to one point of \(J_l\).
By \eqref{fg:eq:capacity},
\[
\inf_{\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\mathrm{d}_\rho(e_i)
\geq\inf_{\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\rho(e_i)>0
\quad\text{for every }i.
\]

Apply Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:correction} separately to each tuple \(\beta\),
using its two assigned elements \(e_{i_+(\beta)},e_{i_-(\beta)}\).
We obtain \(c_\beta\in\mathcal B_\mathrm{sa}\) and
\[
r_{i_\pm(\beta)}
=e_{i_\pm(\beta)}^{1/2}v_{i_\pm(\beta)}\kappa_{S_\beta},
\qquad\left\|r_i\right\|\leq3,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:target-error}
\left\|
f_\beta^*z_\nu f_\beta-
\left(f_\beta^*c_\beta f_\beta
+r_{i_+(\beta)}^*r_{i_+(\beta)}
-r_{i_-(\beta)}^*r_{i_-(\beta)}\right)\right\|
<3\cdot2^{-m}.
\end{equation}

Define \(G,h\) by \eqref{fg:eq:series-overview}; the bound
\(\left\|r_i\right\|\leq3\) gives \(\left\|G\right\|\leq6\).
Let
\[
\mathcal D=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,u,h).
\]
Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:extraction} gives
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:internal-recovery}
r_i=2^i\phi_i h\,d_{S_i}\in\mathcal D,\qquad
G\in\mathcal D,\qquad y=h-G\in\mathcal D.
\end{equation}
In particular, \(\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal D\), so every expression in parentheses
in \eqref{fg:eq:target-error} belongs to \(\mathcal D\).

Fix \(\nu,j,k,\zeta\) and let \(m\to\infty\).
Norm closure and \eqref{fg:eq:target-error} yield
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:quadratics}
(\theta_j+\zeta\theta_k)^*z_\nu
(\theta_j+\zeta\theta_k)\in\mathcal D.
\end{equation}
For self-adjoint \(a,b,z\), the polarization identity is
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:polarization}
azb=\frac14\sum_{\zeta\in\Omega}\overline{\zeta}\,
(a+\zeta b)^*z(a+\zeta b).
\end{equation}
Expanding the sum proves the identity: the coefficient of \(azb\)
is \(4\), while the diagonal coefficients and the coefficient
of \(bza\) vanish because
\(\sum_{\zeta\in\Omega}\overline{\zeta}
=\sum_{\zeta\in\Omega}(\overline{\zeta})^2=0\).
Equation \eqref{fg:eq:quadratics} therefore gives
\(\theta_jz_\nu\theta_k\in\mathcal D\).
Using \eqref{fg:eq:partition},
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:dense-targets}
z_\nu=\sum_{j,k=0}^{22}
\theta_j(\theta_jz_\nu\theta_k)\theta_k\in\mathcal D.
\end{equation}
Thus \(\mathcal D=A\).

Choose \(R=\left\|y\right\|+7\). Since \(h=y+G\) and \(\left\|G\right\|\leq6\),
\(H=R1+h\geq1\). Put \(g=uH\). Then \(g^*g=H^2\), so
functional calculus gives
\[
H=|g|,\qquad u=gH^{-1},\qquad h=H-R1
\]
inside \(\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g)\). Consequently
\(\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,g)=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(1,u,h)=A\).
Also \(1\in \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(g)\): a continuous function equal to one on
\(\sigma(g^*g)\subseteq[1,\infty)\) and zero at zero gives the unit
by nonunital functional calculus. Hence \(\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(g)=A\).

title: Proof
body_md:
Split \(p=q+r\) in \(D\) with \(\tau(q)=\tau(r)\), and choose
\(w\in qMr\) with \(ww^*=q\) and \(w^*w=r\). By Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}, choose self-adjoint generators
\(s,t\) of \(qMq\). Put
\[
Z_0=s+w^*tw+w+w^*.
\]
The algebra \(\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(pD,Z_0)\) contains \(q,r\). Its compressions
recover \(s,w,w^*tw\), hence \(t\), all of \(qMq\), and the
matrix units \(q,r,w,w^*\). They generate \(pMp\). Rescale
\(Z_0\) to obtain a contraction.

label: fg:lem:factor-perturbation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:factor-perturbation}
For every \(\tau\in K\), \(\mathbf b\in A_\mathrm{sa}^{23}\), and
\(\eta>0\), there are \(\widetilde b_j\in(M_\tau)_\mathrm{sa}\) such that
\[
\left\|\widetilde b_j-\pi_\tau(b_j)\right\|<\eta\quad(0\leq j\leq22),
\qquad
\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}\left(u_\tau,\sum_j\psi_j(u_\tau)\widetilde b_j
                          \psi_j(u_\tau)\right)=M_\tau.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppress the representation map in this fibre and put
\(y_0=\sum_j\psi_jb_j\psi_j\). The sets
\(\{\psi_j>1/2\}\) cover the circle. Partition it into
sufficiently short equal-length arcs, with spectral projections
\(p_1,\ldots,p_L\in D\). Choose the partition so that each arc
closure, and each consecutive pair of closures, lies in one of
these sets.

Since \(\mu_\tau\) is atomless, the maximum measure of an arc
of length at most \(1/L\) tends to zero. Indeed, otherwise a
sequence of shrinking arcs with a positive lower measure bound
has centers converging to an atom. Full support makes every
\(p_i\) nonzero, and endpoints have measure zero. Applying
\eqref{eq:main-compression} to the element \(y_0\) of the original
algebra, enlarge \(L\) so that
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:small-diagonal}
\left\|p_i(y_0-\mathbb E_D(y_0))p_i\right\|<\eta/16
\quad(1\leq i\leq L).
\end{equation}
This choice is made only in the fixed fibre.

For each \(i\), choose \(j_i\) with \(\psi_{j_i}>1/2\) on its
arc, and take \(Z_i\) from Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:corner}. For
\(0<\delta<\eta/16\), put
\[
\Delta_i=p_i\mathbb E_D(y_0)p_i+\delta Z_i-p_iy_0p_i.
\]
Its norm is less than \(\eta/8\). The inverse
\(a_i=(p_i\psi_{j_i}p_i)^{-1}\) in the \(p_i\)-corner has norm
at most two. Add \(a_i\Delta_i a_i\) to coordinate \(j_i\).
For each coordinate, the additions occupy orthogonal diagonal
blocks, so their sum has norm less than \(\eta/2\). The new
localized image \(Y_0\) satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:installed-diagonal}
p_iY_0p_i=p_i\mathbb E_D(y_0)p_i+\delta Z_i.
\end{equation}

For each zero consecutive block \(p_iY_0p_{i+1}\), choose a
small nonzero \(s_i\in p_iMp_{i+1}\). A label \(h_i\) has
\(\psi_{h_i}>1/2\) on both arcs. Using the corresponding corner
inverses, add
\[
a_{i,h_i}s_i a_{i+1,h_i}
+a_{i+1,h_i}s_i^*a_{i,h_i}
\]
to coordinate \(h_i\). It inserts precisely \(s_i+s_i^*\)
in those off-diagonal blocks. Choose the finitely many insertions
with total norm less than \(\eta/2\) in each coordinate. They
leave \eqref{fg:eq:installed-diagonal} unchanged.

The resulting image \(Y\), together with \(u\), generates a
von Neumann algebra containing \(D\), every \(p_i\), and
\(p_i\mathbb E_D(y_0)p_i\). Hence it recovers every \(Z_i\) and contains
every full diagonal corner. The consecutive blocks are nonzero;
Lemma~\ref{gr:lem:join} proves that this algebra is \(M\).
All coordinate changes have norm less than \(\eta\).
