label: fg:lem:trace-separation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:trace-separation}
The tuples \(\mathbf b\) for which
\(\tau\mapsto\tau(y_{\mathbf b})\) is injective on \(K\)
form a norm-dense \(G_\delta\) subset of \(A_\mathrm{sa}^{23}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the bounded real-linear map
\[
\mathcal E:A_\mathrm{sa}^{23}\to \mathrm{C}(K,\mathbb R),
\qquad\mathcal E(\mathbf b)(\tau)=\tau(y_{\mathbf b}).
\]
It is an open surjection. Extend \(f\in \mathrm{C}(K,\mathbb R)\) to
a continuous affine function on \(\mathrm{T}(A)\) by integrating against
the representing measures of the Bauer simplex. For every
\(\varepsilon>0\), \cite[Proposition 2.7]{TracialComplete}
gives \(a=a^*\in A\) with
\(\tau(a)=f(\tau)\) and \(\left\|a\right\|\leq\left\|f\right\|_\infty+\varepsilon\).
Set \(b_j=S^{-1/2}aS^{-1/2}\) for all \(j\). Traciality gives
\[
\tau(y_{\mathbf b})
=\tau\left(aS^{-1/2}\Bigl(\sum_j\psi_j(u)^2\Bigr)S^{-1/2}\right)
=\tau(a),
\]
and \(\max_j\left\|b_j\right\|\leq\left\|a\right\|\). These bounds prove openness.

Fix a compatible metric on \(K\). For each \(m\), the condition
\(f(\tau)\neq f(\sigma)\) whenever
\(\operatorname{dist}(\tau,\sigma)\geq1/m\) defines an open
subset \(V_m\) of \(\mathrm{C}(K,\mathbb R)\), by compactness of that
set of pairs. It is dense: choose a finite clopen partition
of mesh less than \(1/m\) on which the oscillation of a given
function is small, then choose distinct nearby constants on
the cells. Thus \(\bigcap_m\mathcal E^{-1}(V_m)\) is a
norm-dense \(G_\delta\), and it is exactly the claimed locus.
head: environment

label: fg:prop:background
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: fg:eq:fibre-polynomials
title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a norm-dense sequence \((z_\nu)\) in the self-adjoint unit
ball of \(A\), and a countable dense family \(\mathcal P\) of
self-adjoint \(*\)-polynomials in \(u,u^*,y\) with coefficients in
\(\mathbb Q+i\mathbb Q\). For \(\nu,k\geq1\), let \(U_{\nu k}\) consist of
tuples \(\mathbf b\) such that
\begin{equation}\label{fg:eq:fibre-polynomials}
\text{for every }\tau\in K\text{ there is }P\in\mathcal P
\text{ with }\left\|z_\nu-P(u,u^*,y_{\mathbf b})\right\|_{2,\tau}<1/k.
\end{equation}
Compactness reduces the witnesses for a fixed tuple to finitely
many polynomials. Equivalently, for some \(P_1,\ldots,P_L\),
\[
\max_{\tau\in K}\min_{1\leq\ell\leq L}
\left\|z_\nu-P_\ell(u,u^*,y_{\mathbf b})\right\|_{2,\tau}<1/k.
\]
This strict inequality is stable under small norm perturbations,
so \(U_{\nu k}\) is open.

Fix \(\mathbf b\) and a norm radius \(r>0\). For each
\(\tau\in K\), apply Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:factor-perturbation}
with \(\eta<r/8\). The perturbed image \(Y\) generates
\(M_\tau\) together with \(u_\tau\). The Kaplansky density theorem gives
a polynomial \(P_\tau\in\mathcal P\) with error less than
\(1/(4k)\) at \(\tau\).
Approximate each difference
\(\widetilde b_j-\pi_\tau(b_j)\) in \(2\)-norm by a
self-adjoint element of \(\pi_\tau(A)\) of norm at most
\(\eta\). Lift it to \(A\) with the same norm by
Lemma~\ref{lem:lift}. Polynomial continuity on bounded sets
gives a tuple \(\mathbf b^{(\tau)}\in A_\mathrm{sa}^{23}\), within
\(r/8\) of \(\mathbf b\), whose \(P_\tau\)-error is less than
\(1/(2k)\) at \(\tau\). This error bound persists on a
neighborhood of \(\tau\).

Choose finitely many of these neighborhoods and a subordinate
clopen partition \(V_1,\ldots,V_L\). Let \(p_\ell=1_{V_\ell}\)
in the center of \(\mathcal M_K\), and let
\(\mathbf b^{(\ell)},P_\ell\) be the corresponding data.
For each coordinate put
\[
\Delta_j=\sum_\ell p_\ell(b_j^{(\ell)}-b_j)
\in\mathcal M_K,\qquad \left\|\Delta_j\right\|\leq r/8.
\]
The localized image of \((b_j+\Delta_j)_j\) agrees with
\(y_{\mathbf b^{(\ell)}}\) in every fibre over \(V_\ell\).
Choose self-adjoint \(c_j\in A\), \(\left\|c_j\right\|\leq r/8\),
approximating \(\Delta_j\) as closely as required in uniform
\(2\)-norm. The bounded density and lifting facts in
Section~\ref{sec:prelim} apply even when the trace family has
a kernel. The finitely many polynomial errors are controlled
uniformly by Lemma~\ref{lem:polynomial}. Thus
\((b_j+c_j)_j\) lies in \(U_{\nu k}\) and in the prescribed
norm neighborhood. This proves density.

Baire's theorem, together with Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:trace-separation},
gives a norm-dense \(G_\delta\) satisfying (i) and all conditions
\eqref{fg:eq:fibre-polynomials}. For such a tuple and fixed
\(\tau\), let \(N_\tau=\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(u_\tau,\pi_\tau(y))\).
Every \(\pi_\tau(z_\nu)\) belongs to \(L^2(N_\tau)\).
The trace-preserving conditional expectation \(\mathbb E_{N_\tau}\)
therefore fixes \(\pi_\tau(A)\), proving (ii). Conversely,
fibrewise generation gives all the polynomial conditions, so
this describes the stated locus exactly.

The restrictions of the extreme traces to \(\mathcal B\) are distinct
by (i), and their GNS closures are the factors \(M_\tau\) by
(ii). Lemma~\ref{lem:separated-fibres} proves (iii), since
\(\left\|\cdot\right\|_{2,K}=\left\|\cdot\right\|_{2,\mathrm{T}(A)}\).

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:capacity}
For every nonzero \(f\in \mathrm{C}(\mathbb T)_+\),
\[
\min_{\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)}\rho(f(u))>0.

In particular, \eqref{fg:eq:capacity} holds.

title: Proof

Full spectral support gives \(\tau(f(u))>0\) for every
\(\tau\in K\). The function \(\tau\mapsto\tau(f(u))\) is
continuous on compact \(K\), hence has a positive minimum.
Every trace is a barycenter of extreme traces, so this lower
bound holds throughout \(\mathrm{T}(A)\).

label: lem:free-word-bound
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We use the creation, diagonal, and annihilation decomposition on the
free-product Hilbert space.
Let \(P_i\) be the projection onto the reduced tensors whose first
letter comes from \(L^2(M_i)\ominus\mathbb C1\). For a centered
\(a\in M_i\), left multiplication decomposes as
\[
 a=C(a)+\Delta(a)+A(a),\qquad
 C(a)=P_i aP_i^\perp,\quad
 \Delta(a)=P_i aP_i,\quad A(a)=P_i^\perp aP_i.
\]
Creation prepends the vector \(a\), so
\(\left\|C(a)\right\|=\left\|a\right\|_2\). Annihilation is the adjoint of
creation by \(a^*\), so traciality gives
\(\left\|A(a)\right\|=\left\|a\right\|_2\); also
\(\left\|\Delta(a)\right\|\leq\left\|a\right\|\).
If two adjacent letters belong to different factors, the products
\(AC\), \(A\Delta\), \(\Delta C\), and \(\Delta\Delta\)
vanish, since \(P_0P_1=0\). Thus the expansion of
\(a_1\cdots a_n\) has only the \(n+1\) terms consisting of
creations followed by annihilations, and the \(n\) terms with one
diagonal operator between creations and annihilations. Taking norms
and summing gives \eqref{eq:free-word-bound}.

label: prop:free-product-compression
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The GNS closure \(M\) is the von Neumann free product of
\(M_0\) and \(M_1=\pi_\sigma(B)''\), with their normal trace
extensions. Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:free-word-bound} applies also when
the endpoint letters involve projections in \(D\subseteq M_0\).
Uniqueness of trace-preserving conditional expectations gives
\(\mathbb E_D^M=\mathbb E_D^{M_0}\circ\mathbb E_{M_0}^M\).
In particular, its restriction to \(M_0\) is
\(\mathbb E_D^{M_0}\). The algebraic free product is spanned by
\(A_0\) and the mixed reduced words
\[
 w=c_0b_1c_1\cdots b_mc_m,\qquad m\geq1,
\]
where \(b_j\in B\) and \(c_j\in A_0\), all \(b_j\) and all
interior \(c_j\) are centered, and the endpoints may be arbitrary,
including \(1\). Freeness gives \(\mathbb E_{M_0}^M(w)=0\),
hence \(\mathbb E_D^M(w)=0\).

Put \(n=2m+1\) and
\(K_w=\prod_{j=0}^m\left\|c_j\right\|\prod_{j=1}^m\left\|b_j\right\|\).
For a projection \(p\in D\), let \(s=\tau(p)\) and write
\[
 pc_0=z_0+\alpha1,\qquad c_mp=z_m+\beta1,
 \qquad \tau(z_0)=\tau(z_m)=0.
\]
Centering is an orthogonal projection in \(L^2\), and traciality
gives
\[
 \left\|z_0\right\|_2\leq\sqrt{s}\left\|c_0\right\|,\quad
 \left\|z_m\right\|_2\leq\sqrt{s}\left\|c_m\right\|,\quad
 |\alpha|\leq s\left\|c_0\right\|,\quad |\beta|\leq s\left\|c_m\right\|,
\]
while \(\left\|z_0\right\|\leq2\left\|c_0\right\|\) and
\(\left\|z_m\right\|\leq2\left\|c_m\right\|\).
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:free-word-bound} to the word with both
endpoints centered. Each of its \(2n+1\) operator summands
has at least one endpoint measured in \(L^2\), because at most
one letter is measured in operator norm. Each summand is therefore
bounded by \(2K_w\sqrt{s}\). The two terms with one scalar
endpoint are bounded by \(2K_ws\) each, and the term with two
scalar endpoints is bounded by \(K_ws^2\), using the ordinary
product norm estimate. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mixed-word-compression}
 \left\|pwp\right\|\leq(4n+7)K_w\sqrt{\tau(p)}.
\end{equation}
This estimate also covers words that begin or end in \(B\), by
taking the corresponding \(c_j=1\).

For \(a\in A\), choose a finite sum \(a'=a_0+\sum_j w_j\)
of this form with \(\left\|a-a'\right\|<\eta\). Contractivity gives
\[
 \left\|p(a-\mathbb E_D^M(a))p\right\|
 \leq2\eta+
 \left\|p(a_0-\mathbb E_D^{M_0}(a_0))p\right\|
 +\sum_j\left\|pw_jp\right\|.
\]
The last two terms tend uniformly to zero as \(\tau(p)\to0\),
by \eqref{eq:base-compression} and
\eqref{eq:mixed-word-compression}. Letting \(\eta\to0\)
proves \eqref{eq:product-compression}.

label: fg:lem:one-trace
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{fg:lem:one-trace}
Let \(A\) be unital with a trace \(\tau\), and suppose it has
comparison by \(\tau\) as in \eqref{eq:factor-comparison}.
If \(A\) contains a \(\tau\)-Haar unitary, then
\(\mathrm{T}(A)=\{\tau\}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix \(\rho\in \mathrm{T}(A)\), and let \(\nu\) be the spectral
distribution of the Haar unitary \(u\) for \(\rho\). An open
arc \(I\) of normalized length \(t\in(0,1)\) is the positivity
set of a continuous positive function \(f_I\). Thus
\[
\mathrm{d}_\tau(f_I(u))=t,\qquad \mathrm{d}_\rho(f_I(u))=\nu(I).
\]
Rotation averaging gives
\(\int_{\mathbb T}\nu(zI)\,dm(z)=t\). Hence some rotation
has measure at most \(t\), and some has measure at least \(t\).

For \(a\in A_+\), put \(s=\mathrm{d}_\tau(a)\in[0,1]\). If \(t>s\),
compare \(a\) with a rotated arc cutoff of \(\rho\)-dimension
at most \(t\); then \(\mathrm{d}_\rho(a)\leq t\). If \(t<s\), compare
a rotated cutoff of \(\rho\)-dimension at least \(t\) with
\(a\); then \(\mathrm{d}_\rho(a)\geq t\). Letting \(t\) approach \(s\),
with the evident one-sided argument at \(0\) and \(1\), gives
\(\mathrm{d}_\rho(a)=\mathrm{d}_\tau(a)\).
Applying this equality to all cutdowns and using
\[
\rho(a)=\int_0^{\left\|a\right\|}\mathrm{d}_\rho((a-t)_+)\,dt
\]
gives \(\rho(a)=\tau(a)\) for all positive \(a\), hence
\(\rho=\tau\).

label: fg:cor:single-trace
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{fg:cor:single-trace}
Let \(A\) be separable and unital with a faithful trace \(\tau\).
Suppose \(M=\pi_\tau(A)''\) is a \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor,
every nonzero corner of \(M\) has two self-adjoint von Neumann
generators, and \(u\in A\) is Haar. Assume comparison by \(\tau\)
and the small-compression condition of Theorem~\ref{thm:polar}
in this GNS representation. Then
\(A=\ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}(u(R1+h))\) for \(h=h^*\) and \(R>\left\|h\right\|\).

name: Single faithful factorial trace

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{fg:lem:one-trace} gives
\(\partial\mathrm{T}(A)=\{\tau\}\). All the
hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:polar} hold.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \((A,\tau)=(A_0,\tau_0)*(B,\sigma)\). The unitary \(v\)
is centered in \(B\), while \(u,u^2\) are centered in \(A_0\)
and satisfy \(\tau_0(u^*u^2)=0\). Since the states are tracial,
these unitaries lie in their centralizers. They satisfy the Avitzour
condition, with the factors interchanged. By
\cite[Theorem~A and Corollary~B]{FloresKlisseOCobhthaighPagliero},
\(A\) is simple, its free-product trace \(\tau\) is its unique
tracial state (indeed, its unique normalized \(2\)-quasitrace),
and it has strict comparison. Thus \textup{(C)} holds and
\(\partial\mathrm{T}(A)=\{\tau\}\). The trace is faithful,
and the image of \(u\) remains Haar. Proposition~\ref{prop:free-product-compression}
gives Condition~\ref{u-cond-2} in \(\pi_\tau(A)''\).
Theorem~\ref{thm:polar} now gives single generation.

title: Remark
body_md:
The compression assumption on a general distinguished factor is
substantive. For example, in
\(A_0=\mathrm{C}([0,1])\otimes\mathrm{M}_2\), with trace
\(\lambda\otimes\operatorname{tr}_2\), the Haar unitary
\(u(t)=e^{2\pi it}1\) generates
\(D=L^\infty([0,1],\lambda)\otimes1\). For
\(a_0=1\otimes e_{12}\), one has
\(\mathbb E_D^{M_0}(a_0)=0\), whereas
\(\left\|pa_0p\right\|=1\) for every nonzero projection
\(p=1_S\otimes1\in D\), even as \(\lambda(S)\to0\).
Thus the existence of a Haar unitary alone does not verify that
assumption. Corollary~\ref{cor:free-product} concerns faithful
tracial states; arbitrary pointed \ensuremath{\mathrm{C}^*}-algebras need not satisfy
the tracial hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:polar}.

title: Proof
body_md:
For \(A_0=\mathrm{C}(\mathbb T)\) with Haar trace, take
\(u(z)=z\). Then \(u\) is Haar and
\(\ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(u)=L^\infty(\mathbb T)=\pi(A_0)''\), so the
compression assumption in Corollary~\ref{cor:free-product} holds
with zero error. Apply that corollary to the standard reduced-free-product
presentation of \(\mathrm{C}_r^*(\mathbb F_n)\), separating one cyclic factor
from the remaining factors. Their reduced free product has a
faithful trace and contains a Haar unitary, also for \(n=\infty\).

For \(A_0=\mathrm{C}([0,1])\) with Lebesgue trace, take
\(u(t)=e^{2\pi it}\). This is a Haar unitary and
\[
 \ensuremath{\mathrm{W}^*}(u)=L^\infty([0,1],\lambda)=\pi_\lambda(A_0)''.
\]
Indeed, \(t\mapsto e^{2\pi it}\) is injective off a null set
and has a measurable inverse there. Hence the compression
assumption again holds with zero error. Group the first interval
factor against the remaining factors and apply
Corollary~\ref{cor:free-product}. This applies to finite and
countably infinite products. In fact, it gives single generation
of \((\mathrm{C}([0,1]),\lambda)*(B,\sigma)\) for every
\((B,\sigma)\) as in that corollary.

title: Proof
body_md:
Put \(A=\mathrm{C}(X,B)\), and let \(u\) be the constant function with
value the unitary in \(B\). Every trace on \(A\) is of the form
\(\mu\otimes\tau\), with \(\mu\in\operatorname{Prob}(X)\).
Indeed, for \(f\in \mathrm{C}(X)_+\), the functional
\(b\mapsto\rho(f\otimes b)\), after normalization when nonzero,
is a trace on \(B\), hence equals \(\tau\). It follows that
\(\rho(f\otimes b)=\rho(f\otimes1)\tau(b)\), and density of
elementary tensors proves the assertion. Therefore
\(\partial\mathrm{T}(A)\cong X\), with extreme traces
\(\tau_x(a)=\tau(a(x))\).

The spectral and compression conditions hold in each fibre by the
assumptions on \(B\). Atomlessness makes each GNS fibre a
\(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor with separable predual, and its nonzero
corners have two self-adjoint generators by Theorem~\ref{thm:SG}.
To check comparison, suppose \(a,b\in A_+\) satisfy its strict
trace inequalities. At each \(x\in X\), comparison in \(B\)
gives, for a prescribed \(\varepsilon>0\), an element \(v_x\in B\)
with
\[
\left\|v_x^*b(x)v_x-a(x)\right\|<\varepsilon/2.
\]
Continuity gives the inequality with \(\varepsilon\) on a
neighborhood of \(x\). Choose a subordinate finite clopen
partition and use the corresponding constant witnesses on
its cells. They define \(v\in \mathrm{C}(X,B)\) with
\(\left\|v^*bv-a\right\|<\varepsilon\). Since \(\varepsilon\) is
arbitrary, \(a\precsim b\). Theorem~\ref{thm:polar} applies.
For the reduced free products, the proof of
Corollary~\ref{cor:free-product} verifies all the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{thm:polar} with a unique trace.
